features.name: Production CSS inlining
features.summary: Inlining puts the page's CSS in a <style> tag in the HTML instead of linking a stylesheet.
features.whatHtml: Inlining puts the page's CSS in a <style> tag in the HTML instead of linking a stylesheet. In principle that removes one render-blocking stylesheet request from the critical path; frameworks without it (Waku, Ember) still link the built stylesheet.
features.gotchasHtml: • A ?inline import puts the whole stylesheet in every HTML response, so it only suits small stylesheets.

features.name: Font optimization
features.summary: A web font is discovered late: the browser finds it only after the CSS that names it has loaded.
features.whatHtml: A web font is discovered late: the browser finds it only after the CSS that names it has loaded. Font optimization self-hosts the files, generates the @font-face rules, and can preload the file. In principle, self-hosting the font (via either route) removes a cross-origin request from the critical path.
features.gotchasHtml: • Importing Fontsource alone does not preload anything. Without a <link rel="preload"> the browser finds the font only after the stylesheet is parsed.

features.name: Image pipeline
features.summary: An image pipeline resizes and re-encodes images per device, emits srcset/sizes, and often adds lazy loading and a blur placeholder.
features.whatHtml: An image pipeline resizes and re-encodes images per device, emits srcset/sizes, and often adds lazy loading and a blur placeholder. In principle this item affects LCP more than FCP.
features.gotchasHtml: • Unpic only builds URLs; something (IPX, a host CDN) still has to serve the resized image.

features.name: Data/HTML caching
features.summary: Caching stores the result of a catalog query or a rendered HTML page so a request does not hit the database again.
features.whatHtml: Caching stores the result of a catalog query or a rendered HTML page so a request does not hit the database again. In principle it shortens time to first byte. A cache that lives in isolate memory does not persist across isolates on a host like Workers, so a portable setup needs persistent KV, Blobs, or Cache-API storage; this repo hand-writes host-specific caches for that reason.
features.gotchasHtml: • Host cache layers differ (Vercel runtime cache, Netlify Blobs, Cloudflare KV), so a "cache" written for one host needs a storage driver for the others.

features.name: Route prefetching
features.summary: Prefetching loads a route's code and data before the click, on hover, focus, or when the link enters the viewport.
features.whatHtml: Prefetching loads a route's code and data before the click, on hover, focus, or when the link enters the viewport. In principle it helps the next navigation rather than the first paint, so it matters for how fast the app feels once someone starts clicking.
features.gotchasHtml: • Prefetching spends bandwidth on routes the user may never visit; intent (hover/focus) is the conservative setting.

features.name: Streaming SSR
features.summary: Streaming SSR sends the HTML in pieces.
features.whatHtml: Streaming SSR sends the HTML in pieces. The server flushes the page shell (<head>, layout, loading placeholders) as soon as it is rendered, and sends each slow part when its data resolves. A buffered server waits for the slowest query before it sends the first byte, so one slow query delays the stylesheet, the fonts, and first paint. The row is ✅ when the framework's own server renderer can flush the shell before all data is ready, with a documented way to mark the deferred parts. In-order streaming counts the same as out-of-order streaming.
features.gotchasHtml:
• The status code and headers are sent with the shell. A redirect or 404 found after that point cannot change them, so frameworks fall back to a client-side redirect or an error boundary.
  • A cached or prerendered page is already complete, so streaming changes nothing for it. Nuxt turns streaming off for routes with cache, isr, or swr rules.
  • A proxy or CDN that buffers the response removes the benefit. Check that your host passes chunks through.
  • Nuxt sends bots the buffered HTML by default. Pracht needs full hydration on a streamed route.

features.name: Early Hints / preload headers
features.summary: A Link: </assets/app.css>; rel=preload; as=style response header names a critical asset before the browser has parsed any HTML.
features.whatHtml: A Link: </assets/app.css>; rel=preload; as=style response header names a critical asset before the browser has parsed any HTML. A 103 Early Hints response sends those Link headers while the server is still rendering, so the stylesheet, font, and script requests start during the server's think time. The row is ✅ when the framework adds preload Link headers for its own built assets, or sends the 103 itself, without the app listing assets by hand. Setting a Link header through a generic headers API is 🔧. A CDN such as Cloudflare can turn a cached Link header into a 103 (Cloudflare Early Hints), which is why preload headers count here even when the framework never writes a 103.
features.gotchasHtml:
• Browsers act on a 103 only over HTTP/2 or HTTP/3, and some proxies mistake a 103 for the final response. Pracht keeps earlyHints off by default for that reason.
  • Nginx and Apache cap header size, and a long Link header can be truncated or rejected. SvelteKit keeps linkHeaderPreload off by default and Next caps the length for the same reason.
  • A static 103 can go out before a route decides to redirect. TanStack's dynamic phase waits for the loaders to avoid that.
  • Styles that are already inlined need no preload. Pracht sends no Link header for inlineCss styles.

features.name: Islands / partial hydration / lazy slices
features.summary: Normally every interactive component on a page hydrates, so its JavaScript downloads and runs.
features.whatHtml: Normally every interactive component on a page hydrates, so its JavaScript downloads and runs. Islands, deferred hydration, and server islands keep most of the page as plain HTML and hydrate (or render on demand) only the parts that need it. This merged row takes each framework's best label across the partial-hydration and server-island capabilities.
features.gotchasHtml: • <ClientOnly> and clientOnly skip server rendering; they are not deferred hydration.

features.name: Per-route render modes
features.summary: A render mode decides when a route's HTML is produced: at build time (static), per request (SSR), on the client (SPA), or revalidated on a schedule.
features.whatHtml: A render mode decides when a route's HTML is produced: at build time (static), per request (SSR), on the client (SPA), or revalidated on a schedule. A per-route switch lets a mostly static site keep one dynamic page without changing the whole app.
features.gotchasHtml: • Static modes need an adapter that can serve prerendered output on the host you deploy to.

features.name: Fine-grained client reactivity
features.summary: Fine-grained reactivity limits how much work a state change causes, so only the parts of the UI that read the changed value update.
features.whatHtml: Fine-grained reactivity limits how much work a state change causes, so only the parts of the UI that read the changed value update. Solid, Svelte, and Marko go furthest and write straight to the affected DOM nodes; Vue and Angular update at component granularity (Vue diffs a compiler-optimised virtual DOM); Qwik falls back to a vDOM for structural changes. React gets there with the first-party React Compiler, which memoizes components, values, and JSX at build time so a state change skips the parts of the tree whose inputs did not change. This is an interaction-cost property, not a first-paint one: in principle it shows up in INP and memory on long-lived pages.
features.gotchasHtml:
• The React Compiler is opt-in for every React framework here: nothing changes until you add it to the build.
  • This row says nothing about first paint; do not read it as a loading-speed feature.

features.name: Built-in bundle analysis
features.summary: A bundle analyzer shows which modules make up each JavaScript bundle so you can find large dependencies.
features.whatHtml: A bundle analyzer shows which modules make up each JavaScript bundle so you can find large dependencies. Only the Next port has an analysis step configured (pnpm analyze runs next analyze); none of the other ports do, so the rest of this section is capability only. Vite DevTools ships DevTools for Rolldown (@vitejs/devtools-rolldown), an ecosystem-level analyzer for production builds on Vite 8+. It is available to the ports on Vite 8 (not the Qwik and Fresh ports, which are on Vite 7) and is not counted in these labels.
features.gotchasHtml: • Run the analyzer against a production build; development bundles are not representative.

features.name: Third-party script strategies
features.summary: Third-party scripts (analytics, chat widgets, tag managers) compete with your own code.
features.whatHtml: Third-party scripts (analytics, chat widgets, tag managers) compete with your own code. A loading strategy says when each one loads, for example before hydration, after hydration, or at browser idle time. No first-party script primitive is documented for most frameworks here, so ordering and deferral are left to the app.
features.gotchasHtml: • Without a strategy API, ordering and deferral are your job: put async/defer and placement choices in the tag yourself.

features.name: Portable multi-host deployment
features.summary: A host adapter builds your app into the shape a platform expects (Node server, serverless functions, edge Worker).
features.whatHtml: A host adapter builds your app into the shape a platform expects (Node server, serverless functions, edge Worker). A portable framework ships adapters or presets for several hosts, so you can switch without rewriting. That gap is one reason this repo hand-writes host-specific caches.
features.gotchasHtml: • Presets and adapters change the build output; they don't set up data caching. Most ports here still write their own host-specific cache code (see section 4).

features.name: Service worker / offline support
features.summary: A service worker is a script the browser keeps between visits.
features.whatHtml: A service worker is a script the browser keeps between visits. It can answer requests from a cache it filled earlier. It does nothing for a first visit, because it installs after the page has loaded. On repeat visits it can serve the built JS and CSS without a network round trip, and it can keep pages working offline. The row is ✅ when the framework builds and registers a service worker and gives it the list of built assets to precache.
features.gotchasHtml:
• A service worker has no effect on a first visit, and a cache-first worker can keep serving an old build. Version the cache name (SvelteKit's version) and delete old caches on activate.
  • Precaching every built file downloads routes the visitor may never open.
  • The generic vite-plugin-pwa works in any Vite build but is built around a static index.html. An SSR app still has to wire the navigation fallback by hand, so it is credited only where a framework-specific package exists (@vite-pwa/nuxt, @vite-pwa/astro).
  • Service workers need HTTPS (or localhost), and most integrations disable them in dev.

artDirection.label: manual
artDirection.bodyHtml:
getImageProps() returns per-breakpoint props; you hand-write the <picture> and <source> elements (hence 🔧). getImageProps() is stable (v14.1.0) and the built-in optimizer already negotiates AVIF/WebP from the Accept header; this row scores only whether the framework emits a <picture> for you.

const {
  props: { srcSet: desktop },
} = getImageProps({ ...common, width: 1440, height: 875, quality: 80, src: '/desktop.jpg' })
const {
  props: { srcSet: mobile, ...rest },
} = getImageProps({ ...common, width: 750, height: 1334, quality: 70, src: '/mobile.jpg' })

return (
  <picture>
    <source media="(min-width: 1000px)" srcSet={desktop} />
    <source media="(min-width: 500px)" srcSet={mobile} />
    <img {...rest} style={{ width: '100%', height: 'auto' }} />
  </picture>
)

Adapted from the image docs, where common is { alt: 'Art Direction Example', sizes: '100vw' }.

Set partialPrefetching (needs cacheComponents; 16.3+), pass prefetch={true} on high-value links (<Link>), and optionally add the FastLink mouse-down navigation.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Streaming is built into the App Router. Add a loading.tsx file next to a page, or wrap a slow component in <Suspense>; the fallback is sent with the shell and the content follows in the same response.

import { Suspense } from 'react'

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading feed...</p>}>
      <PostFeed />
    </Suspense>
  )
}

Adapted from the Next streaming guide (imports of the page's own components omitted).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Nothing to enable in the App Router. During prerendering React emits preload headers for fonts, scripts, and stylesheets, and Next adds them to the response. reactMaxHeadersLength caps their total length (default 6000) for proxies that truncate long headers. Next does not document sending a 103 itself.

module.exports = {
  reactMaxHeadersLength: 1000,
}

From the reactMaxHeadersLength docs.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Server Components keep a component's JavaScript out of the browser (server and client components). Every Client Component still hydrates: no hydrate-on-visible/idle/never control is documented (next/dynamic with ssr: false is client-only rendering, not deferred hydration), although React hydrates each <Suspense> boundary as its own unit and prioritizes the one being interacted with (streaming guide). Enabling cacheComponents: true (the same flag as in section 4, enabled here) renders a cached shell and fills request-time holes. That is functionally close to a server island, but the API is an uncached data boundary inside Suspense, not a named island with its own cache entry.
cells.exampleHtml:
Pages and layouts are Server Components by default and send no component JavaScript. Mark only the interactive part with 'use client'. That component still hydrates, but the rest of the page stays server-only.

// app/[id]/page.tsx (Server Component)
import LikeButton from '@/app/ui/like-button'
import { getPost } from '@/lib/data'

export default async function Page({ params }: { params: Promise<{ id: string }> }) {
  const { id } = await params
  const post = await getPost(id)
  return (
    <main>
      <h1>{post.title}</h1>
      <LikeButton likes={post.likes} />
    </main>
  )
}
// app/ui/like-button.tsx
'use client'

import { useState } from 'react'

export default function LikeButton({ likes }: { likes: number }) {
  // …
}

Source: Next.js: Server and Client Components

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Next documents stable per-route exports: without Cache Components, dynamic and revalidate (previous-model guide); with Cache Components, ensureStatic (v16.4.0+; this port sets ensureStatic = 'shell' in the root layout) plus 'use cache' boundaries (see section 4). This port enables Cache Components, where dynamic, revalidate, fetchCache, and dynamicParams are removed (route segment config).
cells.exampleHtml:
With cacheComponents: true, a layout or page exports ensureStatic to say how much of the route must be static. The port sets 'shell' on the root layout, so the App Shell is prerendered and request-specific content streams in behind <Suspense>. 'navigation' would require the whole route to be static.

// app/layout.tsx
import { Suspense } from 'react'
// …
// Every route's App Shell (sidebar, header, Suspense fallbacks) must stay static;
// request-specific content streams in behind Suspense at prefetch/navigation time.
export const ensureStatic = 'shell'

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>
        <Suspense fallback={<HomeLinkFallback />}>
          <HomeLink />
        </Suspense>
        {children}
      </body>
    </html>
  )
}

Source: Next.js: ensureStatic
cells.gotchasHtml: • With Cache Components on, the dynamic, revalidate, fetchCache, and dynamicParams exports are removed and runtime is unsupported; other segment config such as maxDuration and ensureStatic remains. Do not expect export const dynamic to work.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
The first-party React Compiler, switched on with reactCompiler: true (stable since v16.0.0; enabled in this port). Next runs it through the Babel plugin, applied only to files with JSX or hooks; Next 16.4 also has an experimental native Rust build of the compiler, experimental.turbopackRustReactCompiler: true, used alongside reactCompiler: true.

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  reactCompiler: true,
};

From this repo's next-books/next.config.ts (other options omitted).
cells.gotchasHtml: • The native Rust build of the React Compiler (experimental.turbopackRustReactCompiler) is experimental in Next 16.4; the stable path runs the Babel plugin.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
The Turbopack bundle analyzer (guide) shipped in v16.1 as next experimental-analyze and is next analyze as of v16.4.0 (the old name remains an alias). It opens the Turbopack module graph with per-route client/server filtering; --output saves a static report and next analyze export (v16.4.0+) streams the saved data. This port runs 16.4.6 and uses next analyze. The same guide covers the @next/bundle-analyzer plugin for webpack builds.

npx next analyze
npx next analyze --output

From the package bundling guide.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Use next/script with beforeInteractive, afterInteractive, and lazyOnload strategies for the App Router. worker is experimental, pages/-only, and needs experimental.nextScriptWorkers. The experimental @next/third-parties (guide) wraps common embeds.

import Script from 'next/script'

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <>
      <Script src="https://example.com/script.js" strategy="lazyOnload" />
    </>
  )
}

From the Script docs.
cells.gotchasHtml: • Next's worker strategy is experimental and pages/-only.

cells.label: third-party
cells.bodyHtml:
A stable Adapter API (adapterPath, v16.2+) with verified Vercel and Bun adapters; Cloudflare and Netlify "are working on verified adapters" (deploying). They use their own integrations today: OpenNext for Cloudflare and @netlify/plugin-nextjs for Netlify in this port. output: 'standalone' covers self-hosting, though this port does not set it.

const nextConfig = {
  adapterPath: require.resolve('./my-adapter.js'),
}

Adapted from the adapterPath docs.
cells.gotchasHtml: • Next on Cloudflare and Netlify uses adapters that are experimental or maintained by the host.

cells.label: third-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Next has no service worker build step. Its PWA guide hand-writes public/sw.js for push notifications and names the community Serwist package for offline caching. @serwist/next wraps the Next config, compiles your worker, and injects the precache list. Next's own experimental useOffline hook retries failed navigations once the network returns; it is not a service worker.

import withSerwistInit from "@serwist/next";

const withSerwist = withSerwistInit({
  swSrc: "app/sw.ts",
  swDest: "public/sw.js",
});

export default withSerwist({
  // Your Next.js config
});

Adapted from the Serwist getting-started guide (revision and offline-fallback entries omitted).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Set features.inlineStyles: true, but only on this repo's nuxt-books-optimized-max branch; the plain optimized build leaves the global stylesheet linked.

export default defineNuxtConfig({
  features: {
    // Production SSR embeds entry and component CSS in the HTML.
    inlineStyles: true,
  },
});

From this repo's nuxt-books/nuxt.config.ts (nuxt-books-optimized-max branch).
cells.gotchasHtml: • Nuxt keeps inlineStyles off in dev so stylesheet HMR still works; check the production build.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Add the official @nuxt/fonts module. It resolves the fonts used in CSS, downloads them at build time, serves them from your own origin, injects @font-face rules, generates fallback metrics for lower CLS, and can subset.

export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: [
    '@nuxt/fonts',
  ]
})

Adapted from the module page. This port does not use it; it imports @fontsource-variable/geist manually, so the capability exists in the framework even though this repo took the third-party route:

@import '@fontsource-variable/geist';

From this repo's nuxt-books/app/assets/css/main.css (optimized branch).
cells.gotchasHtml: • The official @nuxt/fonts module is first-party, but this port uses Fontsource instead.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Install @nuxt/image (separate official module) and use <NuxtImg preload> on the first covers.

modules: ['@nuxt/image'],
image: {
  provider: isCloudflare ? 'none' : 'auto',
  quality: 82,
},
<NuxtImg :src="source" :sizes="sizes" :preload="priority" :width="400" :height="600" />

From this repo's nuxt-books/nuxt.config.ts (nuxt-books-optimized-max branch) and app/components/BookCover.vue (optimized branch; some props and options omitted).

artDirection.label: first-party
artDirection.bodyHtml:
<NuxtPicture> serves modern formats with a fallback via @nuxt/image; its docs say it does not support multiple image sources, so no breakpoint art direction.

<NuxtPicture
  format="avif,webp"
  src="/nuxt-icon.png"
/>

From the NuxtPicture docs.

cells.gotchasHtml: • IPX does not run on Cloudflare Workers, so this port switches image optimization off there.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Wrap handlers in defineCachedEventHandler (the Nitro v2 API that this Nuxt 4 port runs on, nitropack 2.13.4; Nitro v3 calls it defineCachedHandler), configure nitro.storage.cache, and add a header-only routeRules cache. The optimized branch uses the Vercel runtime cache, and the max branch adds Netlify Blobs and Cloudflare KV drivers.

export default defineCachedEventHandler(
  async event => { /* ... */ },
  {
    getKey: event => hashCacheKey(/* filters from the query */),
    maxAge: 60 * 60,
    name: 'books-count',
    swr: true,
  },
);
routeRules: {
  '/**': { cache: { headersOnly: true, maxAge: 3600 } },
  '/api/**': { cache: false },
},

From this repo's nuxt-books/server/api/books/count.get.ts (optimized branch; handler body elided) and nuxt.config.ts (nuxt-books-optimized-max branch).

cells.label: experimental
cells.bodyHtml:
Use <NuxtLink> prefetch-on="visibility" | "interaction", _payload.json payload prefetch, and experimental.prefetchPreloadTags (experimental, off by default).

<FastLink :prefetch-on="eagerPrefetch ? 'visibility' : 'interaction'" :to="href">
experimental: {
  prefetchPreloadTags: true,
},

From this repo's nuxt-books/app/components/BookCard.vue (FastLink is this repo's wrapper around NuxtLink; class omitted) and nuxt.config.ts (optimized branch; early404 omitted).

cells.label: experimental
cells.bodyHtml:
Set experimental.ssrStreaming: true. The server sends the shell (<head>, styles, preload hints, entry scripts) first and then streams the body with Vue's renderToWebStream. routeRules can switch it off per route.

export default defineNuxtConfig({
  experimental: {
    ssrStreaming: true,
  },
  routeRules: {
    '/no-stream/**': { streaming: false },
  },
})

From the Nuxt experimental features docs.

cells.label: experimental
cells.bodyHtml:
Set experimental.writeEarlyHints: true. Nuxt then writes a 103 with the page's preload links. The docs limit it to the Node server.

export default defineNuxtConfig({
  experimental: {
    writeEarlyHints: true,
  },
})

From the Nuxt experimental features docs.

cells.label: experimental
cells.bodyHtml:
Documented lazy hydration (hydrate-on-visible, -on-idle, -on-interaction, -on-media-query, hydrate-never on Lazy* components, SFC only; on by default; the switch is experimental.lazyHydration) and features.noScripts / noScripts:

<template>
  <div>
    <LazyMyComponent hydrate-on-visible />
  </div>
</template>

Adapted from the components docs. Server components and islands stay experimental: server components and islands render a component with no client JS; prop changes refetch the island (<NuxtIsland>), and props travel as query parameters so island responses can be cached by a CDN. nuxt-client selective hydration works only on local .vue SFCs, and slots passed to nuxt-client components are server-rendered and not interactive.
cells.gotchasHtml: • nuxt-client hydration and Lazy* hydration only work on SFCs; slot content passed to nuxt-client components is not interactive.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
routeRules: globs map to prerender, swr, isr, ssr: false, cache headers, redirects, and proxy rules.

export default defineNuxtConfig({
  routeRules: {
    '/admin/**': { ssr: false },
  },
})

Adapted from the rendering docs. This port uses a header-only cache rule on /** (needed for _payload.json prefetch) and disables caching on /api/**, shown in section 4.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Vue's ref/reactive tracks dependencies and updates the affected effects. Nothing to enable.

const value = ref('');

From this repo's nuxt-books/app/components/BookSearch.vue (optimized branch).

cells.label: experimental
cells.bodyHtml:
nuxt analyze (experimental) builds the app and serves client and Nitro reports; --json writes machine-readable output.

npx nuxt analyze [ROOTDIR] [--serve] [--prerender] [--json]

Adapted from the analyze command docs (other flags omitted). With Nuxt 5 behaviour the Nitro report needs rollup-plugin-visualizer. The non-experimental build.analyze config option also writes a client-bundle report during a normal nuxt build; with the default Vite builder it loads the community rollup-plugin-visualizer, which must be installed in the project (optional peer dependency), so the cell stays 🧪.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
@nuxt/scripts is a separate official module (modules page, GitHub) with per-script strategy and proxying; useScript's partytown option loads a script in a web worker and needs @nuxtjs/partytown installed and configured separately.

const { onLoaded, onError, status } = useScript('https://example.com/sdk.js')

From the useScript docs.
cells.gotchasHtml: • Nuxt's partytown option needs @nuxtjs/partytown installed and configured separately.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Nitro presets cover every host this repo targets (Node, Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare). Vercel and Netlify auto-detect their presets; force Workers explicitly:

nitro: {
  preset: isCloudflare ? 'cloudflare_module' : undefined,
},

From this repo's nuxt-books/nuxt.config.ts (nuxt-books-optimized-max branch).

cells.label: third-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Add the community @vite-pwa/nuxt module (listed in the Nuxt modules directory). It generates the service worker and the precache manifest with Workbox and registers it.

export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['@vite-pwa/nuxt'],
  pwa: {
    /* PWA options */
  },
})

From the Vite PWA Nuxt docs.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Set inlineStyleThreshold high enough (e.g. Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY; the docs define it as the max CSS file length in UTF-16 code units) in vite.config.ts. One line, but you have to know it exists.

sveltekit({
  inlineStyleThreshold: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY,
})

From this repo's svelte-books/vite.config.ts (optimized branch).

cells.label: third-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Import @fontsource-variable/geist (Fontsource). SvelteKit has no first-party font module and does not preload fonts by default; the handle hook's resolve(..., { preload }) filter can add font preloads (not used here), so the font is discovered from the inlined stylesheet.

@import "@fontsource-variable/geist";

From this repo's svelte-books/src/routes/layout.css (optimized branch).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
The framework offers @sveltejs/enhanced-img, a build-time plugin that only optimizes image files present at build. For remote images such as this port's covers the same page points to a CDN and names the community @unpic/svelte, so this port uses Unpic transforms plus an ipx handler (src/lib/server/ipx-handler.ts), disabled on Cloudflare. adapter-vercel also has an images option (not used here). To use the first-party route for local files:

enhancedImages(), // must come before the SvelteKit plugin
<enhanced:img src="./path/to/your/image.jpg" alt="An alt text" />

Adapted from the images docs.

artDirection.label: first-party
artDirection.bodyHtml:
enhanced:img (local files only) is replaced at build time by an <img> wrapped in a <picture> with multiple formats and sizes; that is modern formats, not breakpoint art direction. Setup is the plugin line shown in section 3:

<enhanced:img src="./path/to/your/image.jpg" alt="An alt text" />

From the images docs.

cells.gotchasHtml: • Sharp does not run on Cloudflare Workers, so this port switches image optimization off there.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Use adapter-vercel's per-route isr option, exported as config from a route, as done in src/lib/server/page-isr.ts. SvelteKit also has first-party, host-independent pieces: setHeaders in load for cache-control (this port sets it in src/routes/+layout.server.ts) and per-route prerender. The experimental remote functions only dedupe a query within one request (and share it on the client while it is in use); their prerender variant stores build-time data. This port turns on the remoteFunctions flag but defines no remote functions. A cross-request data cache on other hosts is manual: src/lib/server/catalog-cache.ts with Vercel Cache, Netlify Blobs, and the Workers KV/Cache API paths.

export const catalogIsrConfig = {
  isr: { expiration: CATALOG_CACHE_REVALIDATE_SECONDS, allowQuery: ['page', 'search'] }
} satisfies Config;
// src/routes/+page.server.ts
export const config = catalogIsrConfig;

From this repo's svelte-books/src/lib/server/page-isr.ts and src/routes/+page.server.ts (optimized branch; allowQuery shortened and spread removed).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Set data-sveltekit-preload-data="hover". This repo's FastLink wrapper maps a preload prop to that attribute per link ('hover' or 'off'); the pagination and sidebar links pass it explicitly and book cards pass preload={eagerPrefetch}. The starter template already sets the attribute on <body>, and JS/CSS are preloaded automatically (performance).

<body data-sveltekit-preload-data="hover">

From this repo's svelte-books/src/app.html (optimized branch; class attribute omitted).
cells.gotchasHtml: • Needs the data-sveltekit-preload-data attribute somewhere (the starter template adds it).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Return a promise from a server load without awaiting it (streaming with promises). The page renders with the awaited data, and each promise is streamed to the browser when it resolves; {#await} shows the placeholder.

export async function load({ params }) {
  return {
    comments: loadComments(params.slug),
    post: await loadPost(params.slug)
  };
}

From the SvelteKit load docs (comments omitted).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Set output.linkHeaderPreload: true (SvelteKit 3.0+, default false). Pages that are not prerendered then preload their JS and CSS through the HTTP Link header instead of <link> elements. SvelteKit does not document sending a 103 itself.

sveltekit({
  output: {
    linkHeaderPreload: true,
  },
})

Adapted from the output config docs; the option sits next to inlineStyleThreshold in this repo's svelte-books/vite.config.ts, which does not set it.

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml:
No first-party islands are documented; all interactive components hydrate, though disabling hydration for a whole route is possible (page options):

export const csr = false;

From the page options docs.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Export prerender, ssr, and csr per route (page options).

export const prerender = true;
export const ssr = false;
export const csr = false;

From the page options docs (each is a separate option; combine as needed).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Runes ($state, $derived, $effect). Dependencies are picked up at runtime from whatever a $derived or $effect reads, not by compile-time analysis, and $state proxies trigger granular updates. Nothing to enable.

let isOpen = $state(false);

From this repo's svelte-books/src/lib/features/book/components/MobileBookSidebar.svelte (optimized branch).

cells.label: third-party
cells.bodyHtml: No built-in analyzer; the performance docs suggest rollup-plugin-visualizer in vite.config.ts. Not configured in this port. No config snippet for it was found in the docs.
cells.exampleHtml:
Add rollup-plugin-visualizer after sveltekit() in the Vite config. vite build then writes a treemap of the bundle to stats.html.

// vite.config.ts
import { sveltekit } from '@sveltejs/kit/vite';
import tailwindcss from '@tailwindcss/vite';
import { visualizer } from 'rollup-plugin-visualizer';
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';

export default defineConfig({
	plugins: [
		tailwindcss(),
		sveltekit({ /* … */ }),
		visualizer({ filename: 'stats.html', gzipSize: true })
	]
});

Source: SvelteKit: Performance

cells.label: third-party
cells.bodyHtml: No first-party script primitive is documented; the performance docs point to Partytown's SvelteKit integration (community package @qwik.dev/partytown) for running third-party scripts in a web worker. Otherwise add the tag in app.html or a component and manage ordering yourself. Not configured in this port.
cells.exampleHtml:
Install @qwik.dev/partytown, add its Vite plugin, and print the Partytown snippet in the root layout. Scripts tagged type="text/partytown" then run in a web worker instead of the main thread.

// vite.config.js
import { sveltekit } from '@sveltejs/kit/vite';
import { partytownVite } from '@qwik.dev/partytown/utils';

export default { plugins: [sveltekit(), partytownVite()] };
<!-- src/routes/+layout.svelte -->
<script>
	import { partytownSnippet } from '@qwik.dev/partytown/integration';
</script>

<svelte:head>
	<script>
		// Forward the necessary functions to the web worker layer
		partytown = { forward: ['dataLayer.push'] };
	</script>
	{@html '<script>' + partytownSnippet() + '</script>'}
	<script type="text/partytown" src="https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=YOUR-ID-HERE"></script>
</svelte:head>

Source: Partytown: SvelteKit

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Pick an adapter for Node, Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare, or static output.

const adapter = isCloudflare
  ? cloudflareAdapter
  : process.env.NETLIFY
    ? netlifyAdapter
    : vercelAdapter;
// ...
sveltekit({ adapter: adapter() })

From this repo's svelte-books/vite.config.ts (optimized branch; other options omitted).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Create src/service-worker.js (or src/service-worker/index.ts). SvelteKit bundles it and registers it automatically, and the $service-worker module gives it the built files, the static files, and a version string.

import { build, files, version } from '$service-worker';

const CACHE = `cache-${version}`;
const ASSETS = [...build, ...files];

Adapted from the SvelteKit service workers docs (the install, activate, and fetch handlers that use these are omitted).

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml:
There is no first-party production inlining flag documented in the styling and assets docs (Solid 2 start mode, this port's stack; production output is <link rel="stylesheet"> tags) or in the archived SolidStart v2 CSS and styling docs, so you wire it yourself: import the stylesheet with ?inline (a Vite CSS feature) and render it in a <style> tag.

import appCss from "./app.css?inline";
// ...
<NoHydration>
  <style>{import.meta.env.SSR ? appCss : ""}</style>
</NoHydration>

From this repo's solid-books/src/Document.tsx (optimized branch). NoHydration keeps the CSS string out of the client bundle.

cells.label: third-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Use @fontsource-variable/geist plus an explicit <link rel="preload" as="font"> with the hashed woff2 URL (static assets; no first-party font primitive documented — that page covers /public and asset imports only).

import geistLatin from "@fontsource-variable/geist/files/geist-latin-wght-normal.woff2?url";
// ...
<link rel="preload" as="font" type="font/woff2" href={geistLatin} crossorigin="" />

From this repo's solid-books/src/Document.tsx (optimized branch).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
The Solid team publishes @solidjs/image (npm latest 1.0.0 for Solid 2; 0.x for Solid 1): a SolidImage component plus imagePlugin from @solidjs/image/vite, which resizes and re-encodes local images at build time with sharp, emits srcset, lazy-loads, and supports blur/BlurHash/ThumbHash previews. It is not mentioned on docs.solidjs.com (package README only). This port does not use it, or Unpic; it uses a custom imageSrcset helper plus the per-host Nitro image config and cover preload components. The Vercel half of that Nitro config looks like this:

nitro({
  vercel: {
    config: {
      version: 3,
      images: {
        sizes: IMAGE_WIDTHS,
        formats: ["image/avif", "image/webp"],
      },
    },
  },
}),

From this repo's solid-books/vite.config.ts (optimized branch; domains, remotePatterns, minimumCacheTTL and the Netlify block omitted).

artDirection.label: first-party
artDirection.bodyHtml: SolidImage from the Solid team's @solidjs/image renders a <picture> with one <source> per output format (default webp + jpeg, AVIF available) and a merged srcset; that is modern formats and sizes, not breakpoint art direction. The package is documented in its README only, not on docs.solidjs.com. This port does not use it and builds srcset with its own imageSrcset helper.
artDirection.exampleHtml:
@solidjs/image covers formats but not breakpoints, so write the <picture> in the port's cover component. Wide screens get Goodreads' large cover, and narrow screens keep the medium one.

// src/features/book/components/book-cover.tsx
import { getLargeBookImageUrl } from "@/features/book/book-constants";
import { imageSrcset } from "@/lib/image-cdn";
// …
{(src) => (
  <picture>
    <source
      media="(min-width: 768px)"
      srcset={imageSrcset(getLargeBookImageUrl(src())) ?? getLargeBookImageUrl(src())}
      sizes={props.sizes}
    />
    <img
      alt={props.title}
      class="absolute inset-0 h-full w-full object-cover"
      decoding="async"
      width={COVER_WIDTH}
      height={COVER_HEIGHT}
      sizes={props.sizes}
      srcset={imageSrcset(src())}
      src={src()}
    />
  </picture>
)}

cells.label: third-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Nitro, the server layer under Solid's start mode, caches routes and handlers: routeRules with cache or swr, plus defineCachedHandler. Nitro is maintained by the Nitro project (nitrojs), not the Solid team, so this counts as third-party, the same basis as SolidStart's multi-host cell. Solid Router's first-party query cache dedupes and caches client-side data only. Route pre-rendering covers any route listed in routes or crawled via nitro.prerender. The optimized port configures no cache, so its loaders in src/features/book/book-queries.ts query Postgres on a cold request. Our feature test sets routeRules: { "/feature-tests/caching": { cache: { maxAge: 2 } } } on Nitro 3 beta: the second request inside the TTL returns the same timestamp with x-cache: HIT, and a request after the TTL gets a new one.

routeRules: {
  "/blog/**": { swr: 3600 },
},

Adapted from the Nitro cache docs; the optimized port does not set it.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Solid Router v1 and the 2.0.0-next.21 prerelease this port pins preload on hover (~20ms) and focus by default. In Solid Router 2.0 stable (npm latest 2.0.1) link preloading is opt-in: createRouter({ routes, preloadLinks: intentPreload() }), with tapPreload, viewportPreload and eagerPreload as other strategies. usePreloadRoute is the manual API, and this port's FastLink calls it on hover and focus (and eagerly when its prefetch prop is set), and starts the navigation on mouse-down.

import { useNavigate, usePreloadRoute } from "@solidjs/router";

From this repo's solid-books/src/components/ui/fast-link.tsx (optimized branch).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
With ssr: true, pages stream from the server (choose a rendering mode): the shell is sent first, then one HTML fragment per <Loading> boundary as its data resolves (performance guide).

plugins: [solid({ start: true, ssr: true })],
<Loading fallback={<p>Loading product…</p>}>
  <article>
    <h1>{product().name}</h1>
  </article>
</Loading>

Adapted from the Solid docs (vite.config.ts line and a shortened <Loading> example).

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml:
No first-party preload headers or Early Hints are documented. httpHeader sets a response header during SSR, so you list each asset yourself.

httpHeader("Link", "</fonts/inter.woff2>; rel=preload; as=font", {
  append: true,
});

From the Solid httpHeader reference.

cells.label: experimental
cells.bodyHtml: No first-party islands are documented: released SolidStart v2 reserves experimental.islands and only accepts false (config reference). Solid 2's @solidjs/web has experimental server components (a component returned from a "use server" function and mounted with dynamicComponent; docs), not used by this port. clientOnly skips SSR for a single component, which is not islands.
cells.exampleHtml:
Solid 2's experimental server components replace islands. A "use server" function returns a component, the client mounts it with dynamicComponent, and only the client components passed in as props or children hydrate. Turn it on with serverFunctions: { components: true } on @solidjs/vite-plugin.

// src/routes/story.tsx
import { dynamicComponent } from 'solid-js'

async function getStory(id: number) {
  'use server'
  const story = await db.stories.get(id)
  return (props) => (
    <article>
      <h1>{story.title}</h1>
      <footer>{props.children}</footer>
    </article>
  )
}

export default function StoryPage(props) {
  const Story = dynamicComponent(() => getStory(props.storyId))
  return (
    <Story>
      <ShareBar />
    </Story>
  )
}

Source: Solid: RFC 11, Server components (experimental)

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Route prerendering is set under top-level nitro: { prerender: { routes, crawlLinks } } in v2/vite-plugin setups, and Nitro routeRules can set swr/cache per route (see the snippet in section 4); there is no per-route SSR/SPA switch. For the Solid 2 stack, see deployment (top-level nitro config) and choose a rendering mode (prerender-crawler).

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [solidStart(), nitro()],
  nitro: {
    prerender: {
      routes: ["/", "/about"],
    },
  },
});

From the archived SolidStart v2 route pre-rendering docs (uses @solidjs/start, not this port's @solidjs/vite-plugin setup).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Signals; updates write to the DOM directly without re-running components.

const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = createSignal(false);

From this repo's solid-books/src/components/mobile-book-sidebar.tsx (optimized branch).

cells.label: third-party
cells.bodyHtml: No first-party analyzer is documented (archived SolidStart v2 docs cover asset handling but no analysis step); rollup-plugin-visualizer would be added, not configured here.
cells.exampleHtml:
Add rollup-plugin-visualizer to the port's Vite config. vite build then writes a treemap of the bundle to stats.html.

// vite.config.ts
import { nitro } from 'nitro/vite'
import solid from '@solidjs/vite-plugin'
import { visualizer } from 'rollup-plugin-visualizer'
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    solid({ start: { /* … */ }, ssr: true }),
    nitro({ /* … */ }),
    visualizer({ filename: 'stats.html', gzipSize: true }),
  ],
})

Source: rollup-plugin-visualizer: README

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: No first-party script-loading strategy is documented (head and metadata); Script from @solidjs/meta only emits a <script> tag (reference). Nothing to enable.
cells.exampleHtml:
Write the tags in the port's Document.tsx, next to its inline theme script. For a lazy strategy, add an inline loader that injects the third-party script once the page is idle.

// src/Document.tsx
const themeScript = `(function(){ /* … from the port … */ })();`;
const lazyAnalytics = `addEventListener("load",function(){(window.requestIdleCallback||setTimeout)(function(){var s=document.createElement("script");s.src="https://example-analytics.com/script.js";s.async=true;document.head.appendChild(s);});});`;

export default function Document(props: ParentProps) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        {/* … meta, font preload, inlined CSS from the port … */}
        <script>{themeScript}</script>
        <script src="https://example.com/critical.js" async />

cells.bodyHtml: No service worker support is documented. Put a hand-written sw.js in public/ (styling and assets) and register it yourself; the worker has no list of built assets unless you generate one.
cells.exampleHtml:
Put a hand-written worker in public/ and register it with an inline script in the document, next to the theme script.

// public/sw.js
const CACHE = 'books-v1'; // change the name on each deploy

self.addEventListener('activate', (event) => {
  event.waitUntil(
    caches.keys().then((keys) => Promise.all(keys.filter((k) => k !== CACHE).map((k) => caches.delete(k)))),
  );
});

self.addEventListener('fetch', (event) => {
  const { request } = event;
  if (request.method !== 'GET' || new URL(request.url).origin !== location.origin) return;
  // Network first, so pages stay current. The cached copy answers when offline.
  event.respondWith(
    fetch(request)
      .then((response) => {
        const copy = response.clone();
        caches.open(CACHE).then((cache) => cache.put(request, copy));
        return response;
      })
      .catch(() => caches.match(request)),
  );
});
// src/Document.tsx

// src/server.ts
import { createStartHandler, defaultStreamHandler } from '@tanstack/solid-start/server'
import { createServerEntry } from '@tanstack/solid-start/server-entry'

const processRequest = createStartHandler(defaultStreamHandler)
export default createServerEntry({ fetch: (request, opts) => processRequest(request, opts) })
// src/routes/$id.tsx
import { createFileRoute, Await } from '@tanstack/solid-router'

export const Route = createFileRoute('/$id')({
  loader: async ({ params }) => ({
    book: await getBook(params.id),       // awaited: in the first chunk
    reviews: getReviews(params.id),       // not awaited: streamed later
  }),
  component: BookPage,
})

function BookPage() {
  const data = Route.useLoaderData()
  return (
    <>
      <h1>{data().book.title}</h1>
      <Await promise={data().reviews} fallback={<p>Loading reviews…</p>}>
        {(reviews) => <ul>{reviews.map((r) => <li>{r.text}</li>)}</ul>}
      </Await>
    </>
  )
}

// src/server.ts
import handler from '@tanstack/solid-start/server-entry'
import type { ServerRequest } from 'srvx'

export default {
  fetch(request: Request) {
    const serverRequest = request as ServerRequest
    return handler.fetch(request, {
      onEarlyHints: ({ phase, allLinks }) => {
        if (phase !== 'dynamic') return
        const response = serverRequest.runtime?.node?.res
        if (response?.writeEarlyHints && allLinks.length) {
          response.writeEarlyHints({ link: allLinks })
        }
      },
    })
  },
}

cells.exampleHtml:
The port picks one host plugin at build time: @cloudflare/vite-plugin on Cloudflare, @netlify/vite-plugin-tanstack-start on Netlify, and Nitro everywhere else (Vercel included).

// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig, type PluginOption } from 'vite'
import { tanstackStart } from '@tanstack/solid-start/plugin/vite'
import viteSolid from '@solidjs/vite-plugin'
import { nitro } from 'nitro/vite'

const isCloudflare = Boolean(process.env.CLOUDFLARE || process.env.WORKERS_CI || process.env.CF_PAGES)
const isNetlify = Boolean(process.env.NETLIFY)

export default defineConfig(async () => {
  const plugins: PluginOption[] = []
  if (isCloudflare) {
    const { cloudflare } = await import('@cloudflare/vite-plugin')
    plugins.push(cloudflare({ viteEnvironment: { name: 'ssr' } }))
  } else if (isNetlify) {
    const netlify = (await import('@netlify/vite-plugin-tanstack-start')).default

// src/components/lazy-script.tsx
'use client';
import { useEffect } from 'react';

export function LazyScript({ src }: { src: string }) {
  useEffect(() => {
    const inject = () => {
      if (document.querySelector(`script[src="${src}"]`)) return;
      const s = Object.assign(document.createElement('script'), { src, async: true });
      document.head.append(s);
    };
    const idle = () => ('requestIdleCallback' in window ? requestIdleCallback(inject) : setTimeout(inject));
    if (document.readyState === 'complete') idle();
    else addEventListener('load', idle, { once: true });
  }, [src]);
  return null;
}

The port's build step already rewrites the HTML template. Extend it to swap the built stylesheet <link> for a <style> tag. The Node, Vercel, Netlify and Cloudflare deploys all use that template, so they all get the inlined CSS.

// scripts/prepare-server-template.mjs
import { mkdir, readFile, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { resolve } from 'node:path';

const root = process.cwd();
const clientIndex = resolve(root, 'dist/client/index.html');
const serverTemplate = resolve(root, 'dist/server/template.html');

let html = await readFile(clientIndex, 'utf8');
const link = html.match(/<link[^>]+href="(\/assets\/[^"]+\.css)"[^>]*>/);
if (link) {
  const css = await readFile(resolve(root, 'dist/client', link[1].slice(1)), 'utf8');
  html = html.replace(link[0], `<style>${css}</style>`);
}

await mkdir(resolve(root, 'dist/server'), { recursive: true });
await writeFile(serverTemplate, html);
await rm(clientIndex);

const bookCache = new Map();
export function prefetchBook(id, searchParams) {
  const key = `${id}?${stringifySearchParams(searchParams)}`;
  if (!bookCache.has(key)) bookCache.set(key, loadBook(id, searchParams));
  return bookCache.get(key);
}

// app/modifiers/prefetch-book.js
import { modifier } from 'ember-modifier';
import { prefetchBook } from '../lib/book/load-catalog';

export default modifier((element, [id, searchParams]) => {
  const warm = () => prefetchBook(id, searchParams);
  element.addEventListener('pointerenter', warm, { once: true });
  element.addEventListener('focus', warm, { once: true });
  return () => {
    element.removeEventListener('pointerenter', warm);
    element.removeEventListener('focus', warm);
  };
});

// app/routes/book.js: model(params) { return prefetchBook(params.id, parseSearchParams(params)); }
// app/components/book/book-card.gjs
<LinkTo @route="book" @model={{this.bookId}} @query={{this.query}}
        {{prefetchBook this.bookId @searchParams}}>
  {{! … }}
</LinkTo>

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: No streaming render is documented. The FastBoot user guide and the community vite-ember-ssr layer this port uses both render the whole page and then send it.
cells.exampleHtml:
Return a ReadableStream from the request handler. It sends the top of the HTML template right away, then waits for the Ember render and sends the rest. The status code is fixed at 200 once the first chunk is out.

// server/handle-request.js
import { assembleHTML } from 'vite-ember-ssr/server';

const HEAD_MARKER = '<!-- VITE_EMBER_SSR_HEAD -->';
// … in handleFetch, for page requests
const template = await getTemplate();
const early = template.slice(0, template.indexOf(HEAD_MARKER));
const encoder = new TextEncoder();

const body = new ReadableStream({
  async start(controller) {
    controller.enqueue(encoder.encode(early)); // charset, viewport, favicon
    const emberApp = await getEmberApp();
    const rendered = await emberApp.renderRoute(`${url.pathname}${url.search}`, { settledTimeout: 8000 });
    controller.enqueue(encoder.encode(assembleHTML(template, rendered).slice(early.length)));
    controller.close();
  },
});
return new Response(body, { headers: { 'content-type': 'text/html; charset=utf-8' } });

Source: vite-ember-ssr · MDN: ReadableStream

cells.exampleHtml:
Set a Link header on the Fastify reply that sends the rendered page. This one preconnects to the font host. To preload a built file with a hashed name, read its URL from the Vite manifest.

// server.js
const LINK = '<https://fonts.gstatic.com>; rel=preconnect; crossorigin';
// … in the handler that sends the SSR result
const { html } = await renderHtml(emberApp, request.url, template);
return reply.header('Link', LINK).type('text/html').send(html);

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: Nothing to enable: no first-party partial hydration is documented; SSR is app-wide (community vite-ember-ssr here; official FastBoot).
cells.exampleHtml:
Serve the page with a small entry instead of app/entry.js. Then mount each interactive component into its placeholder with renderComponent from @ember/renderer. The rest of the page stays static HTML.

// app/islands.js (the only <script type="module"> on a static page)
import { renderComponent } from '@ember/renderer';
import FavoriteButton from './components/islands/favorite-button';

const islands = { 'favorite-button': FavoriteButton };

for (const el of document.querySelectorAll('[data-island]')) {
  const args = JSON.parse(el.dataset.args ?? '{}');
  el.replaceChildren(); // no hydration: drop the server markup, then render fresh
  renderComponent(islands[el.dataset.island], { into: el, args });
}

// app/components/islands/favorite-button.gjs
import Component from '@glimmer/component';
import { tracked } from '@glimmer/tracking';
import { on } from '@ember/modifier';

export default class FavoriteButton extends Component {
  @tracked saved = false;
  toggle = () => (this.saved = !this.saved);
  <template>
    <button type="button" {{on "click" this.toggle}}>
      {{if this.saved "Saved" "Save"}} {{@title}}
    </button>
  </template>
}

Source: RFC 1099: renderComponent

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: SSR is app-wide in this port (emberSsr() from community vite-ember-ssr; official FastBoot is also app-wide). vite-ember-ssr can additionally prerender a listed set of routes at build time (emberSsg({ routes })), a community build step (React Router's equivalent first-party prerender list is what earns its ✅); no first-party per-route render mode is documented, so nothing to enable.
cells.exampleHtml:
Choose the mode per path in the port's request handler. Server-render the routes that need it. For the rest, return the unrendered template: the same SPA shell the port's Netlify and Cloudflare deploys serve.

// server/handle-request.js
const CLIENT_ONLY = [/^\/account(\/|$)/]; // example: routes that skip SSR

export async function handleFetch(request, options = {}) {
  const url = new URL(request.url);
  // … /api/* handlers from the port …

  const template = await getTemplate();
  if (CLIENT_ONLY.some((re) => re.test(url.pathname))) {
    // SPA shell: app/entry.js boots the app in the browser
    return new Response(template, {
      headers: { 'content-type': 'text/html; charset=utf-8' },
    });
  }

  const emberApp = await getEmberApp();
  const rendered = await emberApp.renderRoute(`${url.pathname}${url.search}`, {
    settledTimeout: 8000,
  });
  return new Response(assembleHTML(template, rendered), {
    headers: { 'content-type': 'text/html; charset=utf-8' },
    status: rendered.statusCode,
  });
}

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: Embroider/Vite (guide) plus a community SSR layer (vite-ember-ssr here; in this port only the Node server and the Vercel function server-render, while the Netlify and Cloudflare deploys serve a static SPA shell plus API functions). Official FastBoot 6.0.0 documents Ember CLI builds only; Vite-app support is an open draft PR. No first-party host adapters are documented (FastBoot's deploy page covers a Node app server plus Heroku- and community-maintained AWS integrations, not Vercel, Netlify, or Cloudflare), so nothing to enable.
cells.exampleHtml:
From the port: each host gets its own entry file and config, written by hand. Vercel runs the SSR handler as a function (vercel.json rewrites everything to /api). Cloudflare runs a Worker that serves the API and the static SPA shell. Netlify uses netlify.toml redirects plus netlify/functions/api.mjs.

// api/index.js (Vercel: SSR + API)
import '../server/load-env.js';
import { handleNodeRequest } from '../server/handle-request.js';
export default handleNodeRequest;

// workers/index.mjs (Cloudflare: API only, assets from dist/client)
import { bookPayload, catalogPayload, searchParamsFromUrl } from '../server/catalog-api.js';

export default {
  async fetch(request, env) {
    if (env?.POSTGRES_URL) process.env.POSTGRES_URL = env.POSTGRES_URL;
    const url = new URL(request.url);
    if (url.pathname === '/api/catalog') {
      return Response.json(await catalogPayload(searchParamsFromUrl(url.href)));
    }
    // … /api/books/:id …
    return env.ASSETS.fetch(request); // SPA shell (not_found_handling: single-page-application)
  },
};

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: No first-party service worker is documented in the Ember guides. The community ember-service-worker addon was last published in 2020 (9.0.1) and plugs into the classic Ember CLI build, which this Vite port does not use.
cells.exampleHtml:
Put a hand-written worker in public/ and register it with an inline script in index.html.

// public/sw.js
const CACHE = 'books-v1'; // change the name on each deploy

self.addEventListener('activate', (event) => {
  event.waitUntil(
    caches.keys().then((keys) => Promise.all(keys.filter((k) => k !== CACHE).map((k) => caches.delete(k)))),
  );
});

self.addEventListener('fetch', (event) => {
  const { request } = event;
  if (request.method !== 'GET' || new URL(request.url).origin !== location.origin) return;
  // Network first, so pages stay current. The cached copy answers when offline.
  event.respondWith(
    fetch(request)
      .then((response) => {
        const copy = response.clone();
        caches.open(CACHE).then((cache) => cache.put(request, copy));
        return response;
      })
      .catch(() => caches.match(request)),
  );
});
<!-- index.html, before </head> -->
<script>
  if ('serviceWorker' in navigator) {
    addEventListener('load', () => navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js'));
  }
</script>

Source: Using Service Workers (MDN)

build.inlineStylesheets controls whether project CSS ships as <style> tags or linked files. 'always' inlines every stylesheet; the default 'auto' inlines only files under Vite's 4kB assetsInlineLimit.

// astro.config.mjs
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';

export default defineConfig({
  build: {
    inlineStylesheets: 'always', // 'auto' (default) | 'never'
  },

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Fonts API: top-level fonts config (astro@6.0.0+) plus <Font cssVariable preload /> from astro:assets, not under experimental flags. Providers include Google, Bunny, Fontsource, Fontshare, Adobe, local; fonts are downloaded, cached, served from _astro/fonts, with a subsets option (default latin) and optimized fallbacks. preload defaults to false. (fonts, astro-assets)
cells.exampleHtml:
Register the font in the top-level fonts config, then render <Font /> in the layout head. Astro downloads and serves the files itself, and preload adds a preload link.

// astro.config.mjs
import { defineConfig, fontProviders } from 'astro/config';

export default defineConfig({
  fonts: [{
    provider: fontProviders.fontsource(),
    name: 'Roboto',
    cssVariable: '--font-roboto',
  }],
});
---
// src/layouts/Layout.astro
import { Font } from 'astro:assets';
---
<html>
  <head>
    <Font cssVariable="--font-roboto" preload />
  </head>
  <body><slot /></body>
</html>

cells.bodyHtml: <Image /> from astro:assets optimizes local and authorized remote images; Sharp is the default service; responsive layout/srcset since astro@5.10.0; public/ images are not optimized. Cloudflare, Vercel, and Netlify adapters have host image services. (images, cloudflare, vercel, netlify)
cells.exampleHtml:
<Image /> from astro:assets resizes and converts imported local images at build time. layout="constrained" adds a responsive srcset, and image.domains lets remote images through the same pipeline.

---
// src/components/Cover.astro
import { Image } from 'astro:assets';
import cover from '../assets/cover.jpg';
---
<Image src={cover} alt="Book cover" layout="constrained" width={800} height={600} />
// astro.config.mjs
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';

export default defineConfig({
  image: {
    domains: ['covers.example.com'],
  },
});

Source: Astro: Images

artDirection.label: first-party
artDirection.bodyHtml: <Picture /> (astro@3.3.0+) emits <picture> with formats (default webp) plus a fallback <img>. Breakpoint art direction is not in the component docs; the official recipe uses getImage() and a hand-written <picture>/<source media>. (astro-assets, build-custom-img-component)
artDirection.exampleHtml:
<Picture /> handles formats, not breakpoints. Astro's recipe calls getImage() once per crop and writes the <picture> by hand.

---
// src/components/Hero.astro
import { getImage } from "astro:assets";
import wide from "../assets/hero-wide.jpg";
import square from "../assets/hero-square.jpg";

const desktop = await getImage({ src: wide, width: 1600, format: "avif" });
const mobile = await getImage({ src: square, width: 600, format: "webp" });
const fallback = await getImage({ src: square, width: 600 });
---
<picture>
  <source media="(min-width: 768px)" srcset={desktop.src} type="image/avif" />
  <source srcset={mobile.src} type="image/webp" />
  <img src={fallback.src} {...fallback.attributes} alt="Shelves of books" />
</picture>

Source: Astro: build a custom image component

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Route caching for on-demand pages (astro@7.0.0+): top-level cache: { provider } with memoryCache(), Astro.cache.set({ maxAge, swr, tags }), routeRules, cache.invalidate(). Host providers (cacheNetlify(), cacheVercel(), cacheCloudflare()) are experimental and manually enabled. Also Vercel isr: true and Netlify cacheOnDemandPages. (caching, astro-7, vercel, netlify)
cells.exampleHtml:
Pick a cache provider in the config, then set cache options from an on-demand page. routeRules sets defaults for groups of routes, and cache.invalidate() purges by tag or path.

// astro.config.mjs
import { defineConfig, memoryCache } from 'astro/config';

export default defineConfig({
  cache: { provider: memoryCache() },
  routeRules: {
    '/books/[...slug]': { maxAge: 3600, tags: ['books'] },
  },
});
---
// src/pages/index.astro
export const prerender = false;
Astro.cache.set({ maxAge: 120, swr: 60, tags: ['home'] });
---
// src/pages/api/revalidate.ts
import type { APIRoute } from 'astro';

export const POST: APIRoute = async (context) => {
  await context.cache.invalidate({ tags: ['books'] });
  return new Response(null, { status: 204 });
};

Source: Astro: Route caching

Strategies hover (default), tap, viewport, load; falls back to tap on data saver. <ClientRouter /> pages prefetch by default. eagerness and Speculation Rules need experimental clientPrerender. (prefetch)

prefetch: true turns on the prefetch script. Links opt in with data-astro-prefetch and a strategy, or prefetchAll covers every link.

// astro.config.mjs
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';

export default defineConfig({
  prefetch: {
    prefetchAll: true,
    defaultStrategy: 'viewport', // 'hover' (default) | 'tap' | 'viewport' | 'load'
  },

<a href="/books" data-astro-prefetch="tap">Books</a>
<a href="/account" data-astro-prefetch="false">Account</a>

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: On-demand pages use HTML streaming: the document is sent in chunks, in order, as each component renders, so <head> and the top of the page go out before a slow await further down finishes. Nothing to enable. Move slow fetches into child components so they do not block the parts above them; server:defer server islands cover content that should arrive out of order. (on-demand-rendering)
cells.exampleHtml:
On-demand pages stream by default. Put a slow fetch in its own component: the HTML above it is sent while it waits.

---
// src/pages/books/[id].astro
export const prerender = false; // render on demand
import Layout from "../../layouts/Layout.astro";
import BookDetail from "../../components/BookDetail.astro";
import Reviews from "../../components/Reviews.astro";
---
<Layout title="Book">
  <BookDetail id={Astro.params.id} />
  <!-- head, header and BookDetail are already sent while Reviews awaits -->
  <Reviews id={Astro.params.id} />
</Layout>
---
// src/components/Reviews.astro
const res = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/books/${Astro.props.id}/reviews`);
const reviews = await res.json();
---
<ul>{reviews.map((r) => <li>{r.text}</li>)}</ul>

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: No first-party preload Link headers or 103 Early Hints documented; the configuration reference has no option for either. Set a Link header by hand with Astro.response.headers or at the host. (configuration-reference, on-demand-rendering)
cells.exampleHtml:
Set a Link header on HTML responses in the middleware. This one preconnects to the font host. To preload a built file with a hashed name, read its URL from the Vite manifest.

// src/middleware.ts
import { defineMiddleware } from 'astro:middleware'

const LINK = '<https://fonts.gstatic.com>; rel=preconnect; crossorigin'

export const onRequest = defineMiddleware(async (_context, next) => {
  const response = await next()
  if (!response.headers.get('content-type')?.includes('text/html')) return response
  const headers = new Headers(response.headers)
  headers.set('Link', LINK)
  return new Response(response.body, { status: response.status, statusText: response.statusText, headers })
})

Source: Astro middleware

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Zero client JS by default; client:load, client:idle, client:visible, client:media, client:only. server:defer server islands need an adapter; props travel in an encrypted query string. Server islands were experimental in astro@4.12 (experimental.serverIslands) and the flag was removed in astro@5.0, where the feature is available without it; the guide carries no experimental label. (islands, framework-components, server-islands, upgrade-to/v5, astro-4120)

---
// src/pages/index.astro
import Counter from '../components/Counter.jsx';
import Avatar from '../components/Avatar.astro';
import GenericAvatar from '../components/GenericAvatar.astro';
---
<Counter client:visible />

<Avatar server:defer>
  <GenericAvatar slot="fallback" />
</Avatar>

// src/components/Counter.tsx
import { createSignal } from 'solid-js';

export default function Counter() {

  return <button onClick={() => setCount(count() + 1)}>Clicked {count()}</button>;
}

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Official adapters for Node (standalone/middleware), Vercel, Netlify, and Cloudflare; the on-demand rendering page names all four as official, and astro add <adapter> installs them. (on-demand-rendering, deploy, node, vercel, netlify, cloudflare)
cells.exampleHtml:
The Books port picks an official adapter from the build environment and falls back to Node. Each adapter is installed with astro add <name>.

// astro.config.mjs
import node from '@astrojs/node';
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';

async function pickAdapter() {
  if (process.env.NETLIFY) return (await import('@astrojs/netlify')).default();
  if (process.env.CF_PAGES) return (await import('@astrojs/cloudflare')).default();
  if (process.env.VERCEL) return (await import('@astrojs/vercel')).default();
  return node({ mode: 'standalone' });
}

export default defineConfig({
  output: 'server',
  adapter: await pickAdapter(),
});

Source: Astro: @astrojs/node

// app/root.tsx
import appCss from './styles/global.css?inline'

export const links: Route.LinksFunction = () => [
  { rel: 'icon', href: '/icon.svg', type: 'image/svg+xml' },
  // no { rel: 'stylesheet' } entry: the CSS is inlined below
]

export function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        <Meta />
        <Links />
        <style dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: appCss }} />
      </head>
      {/* … */}
    </html>
  )
}

cells.bodyHtml: No first-party font primitive documented; the styling page does not cover fonts (use Fontsource or a CDN by hand). (styling)
cells.exampleHtml:
The port installs Fontsource's variable Geist packages and imports them at the top of the global stylesheet. The packages ship the @font-face rules and self-hosted font files, and Vite bundles them like any other CSS import.

/* app/styles/global.css */
@import '@fontsource-variable/geist';
@import '@fontsource-variable/geist-mono';
@import 'tailwindcss';

@theme {
  /* … */
  --font-geist-sans: 'Geist Variable', 'Geist', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif;
  --font-geist-mono: 'Geist Mono Variable', 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, monospace;
  --font-sans: var(--font-geist-sans);
  --font-mono: var(--font-geist-mono);
}

cells.label: third-party
cells.bodyHtml: No first-party image component or optimizer documented (only a ?url asset import is shown); use a community package such as @unpic/react or a host image CDN by hand. (styling)
cells.exampleHtml:
Install @unpic/react and render its <Image> in place of <img>. When it recognizes the image CDN in the URL, it writes a responsive srcset that asks the CDN for each width. It also sets sizes, dimensions and lazy loading.

// app/features/book/components/book-cover.tsx
import { Image } from '@unpic/react'

export function BookCover({ src, title }: { src: string; title: string }) {
  return (
    <Image
      src={src}
      layout="constrained"
      width={300}
      height={450}
      alt={title}
    />
  )
}

artDirection.label: manual
artDirection.bodyHtml: No first-party <picture> helper documented; hand-write the markup. (styling)
artDirection.exampleHtml:
There is no image component, so write <picture> in a route or component, with files served from public/. React spells the attribute srcSet.

// app/features/home/hero-image.tsx
export function HeroImage() {
  return (
    <picture>
      {/* art direction: a square crop on narrow screens */}
      <source media="(max-width: 640px)" type="image/avif"
              srcSet="/media/hero-square-640.avif" width={640} height={640} />
      {/* format fallback: AVIF, then WebP, then the <img> JPEG */}
      <source type="image/avif" sizes="100vw"
              srcSet="/media/hero-1280.avif 1280w, /media/hero-1920.avif 1920w" />
      <source type="image/webp" sizes="100vw"
              srcSet="/media/hero-1280.webp 1280w, /media/hero-1920.webp 1920w" />
      <img src="/media/hero-1280.jpg" alt="Shelves of books" width={1280} height={720}
           fetchPriority="high" decoding="async" />
    </picture>
  )
}

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Route headers export sets Cache-Control (deepest route wins; parentHeaders merges). prerender config is build-time only, with no ISR/revalidate option. Vercel's docs show s-maxage=1, stale-while-revalidate=59 via headers. (headers, pre-rendering, react-router)
cells.exampleHtml:
Export headers from a route module to set Cache-Control on that route's document response. A child route can read parentHeaders and overwrite one value.

// app/routes/book.tsx
import type { Route } from './+types/book'

export function headers({ parentHeaders }: Route.HeadersArgs) {
  parentHeaders.set(
    'Cache-Control',
    'max-age=3600, s-maxage=86400',
  )
  return parentHeaders
}

Source: React Router: HTTP Headers

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: <Link prefetch="none|intent|render|viewport">, default none, uses <link rel="prefetch">. Lazy route discovery is on by default and batch-discovers rendered links; discover="none" opts out. (Link, lazy-route-discovery, react-router.config.ts)
cells.exampleHtml:
Set prefetch on <Link>. "intent" loads the route module and data on hover or focus, "viewport" when the link scrolls into view, and "render" as soon as it renders. The port wraps <Link> in its own FastLink.

// app/components/ui/fast-link.tsx
import { Link } from 'react-router'
// …
export function FastLink({ href, prefetch = 'intent', ...rest }: Props) {
  return (
    <Link
      prefetch={prefetch === false ? 'none' : prefetch === true ? 'intent' : prefetch}
      to={href}
      {...rest}
    />
  )
}

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Return a promise from a loader without awaiting it, then render it with <Await resolve={...}> inside <Suspense>; the awaited data renders first and the rest streams in. The loader must return an object with keys, not a single promise. (suspense)
cells.exampleHtml:
The loader awaits the critical data and returns the slow promise as-is. The component renders that promise with <Await> inside <Suspense>, so the fallback goes out first.

// app/routes/book.tsx
import { Suspense } from 'react'
import { Await } from 'react-router'
import type { Route } from './+types/book'

export async function loader({ params }: Route.LoaderArgs) {
  const reviews = getReviews(params.id) // NOT awaited
  const book = await getBook(params.id)
  return { book, reviews }
}

export default function Book({ loaderData }: Route.ComponentProps) {
  return (
    <>
      <h1>{loaderData.book.title}</h1>
      <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading reviews…</p>}>
        <Await resolve={loaderData.reviews}>
          {(reviews) => <ul>{reviews.map((r) => <li key={r.id}>{r.text}</li>)}</ul>}
        </Await>
      </Suspense>
    </>
  )
}

Source: React Router: Streaming with Suspense

// app/routes/home.tsx

cells.bodyHtml: Experimental RSC (React 19+): unstable_reactRouterRSC from @react-router/dev/vite plus experimental @vitejs/plugin-rsc; unstable_-prefixed and still unstable in 8.5.2. No islands or partial-hydration primitive documented. splitRouteModules only splits client exports. (react-server-components, code-splitting)

Swap reactRouter() for the unstable RSC plugin and add @vitejs/plugin-rsc after it. Route modules then render as React Server Components, and only 'use client' modules ship JavaScript.

// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import { unstable_reactRouterRSC as reactRouterRSC } from '@react-router/dev/vite'
import rsc from '@vitejs/plugin-rsc'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [reactRouterRSC(), rsc()],

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: prerender (stable config) takes a per-URL list, so listed paths are static while the rest are server-rendered (ssr: true) or served from the SPA fallback (ssr: false); clientLoader skips server data per route. ssr itself is global, with no per-route export; ssr: "unstable_api-only" is experimental (v8.5.0). (rendering, pre-rendering, spa)
cells.exampleHtml:
List the URLs to prerender at build time. Those paths become static HTML, and every other path is server-rendered because ssr stays true.

// react-router.config.ts
import type { Config } from '@react-router/dev/config'

export default {
  // Can be omitted - defaults to true
  ssr: true,
  prerender: ['/', '/blog', '/blog/popular-post'],
} satisfies Config

cells.bodyHtml: React-based; the first-party React Compiler is added as a Babel preset to the React Vite plugin (not enabled in this port). v8.4.0 also split internal router contexts to reduce router re-renders. (react-compiler, changelog)

Add the React Compiler's Babel plugin next to reactRouter(). The compiler memoizes components and hooks at build time, so fewer components re-render when state changes.

import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import babel from 'vite-plugin-babel'
import { reactRouter } from '@react-router/dev/vite'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    reactRouter(),
    babel({
      filter: /\.[jt]sx?$/,
      babelConfig: {
        presets: ['@babel/preset-typescript'],
        plugins: [['babel-plugin-react-compiler', {}]],
      },

  ],
})

cells.bodyHtml: No first-party strategy documented; <Scripts> renders the app runtime and only spreads attributes (crossOrigin, nonce), with no async/defer strategy documented. (Scripts)
cells.exampleHtml:
<Scripts /> only renders the app runtime, so write the tags yourself: async in Layout for early scripts, or inject in a useEffect after hydration.

// app/root.tsx
import { useEffect } from 'react'
// …
export function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        {/* … */}
        {/* React 19 hoists and de-duplicates <script async src> */}
        <script async src="https://plausible.io/js/script.js" data-domain="books.example" />
      </head>
      {/* … */}
    </html>
  )
}

export default function App() {
  useEffect(() => {
    // Client only, after hydration: load the chat widget when the browser is idle.
    ;(window.requestIdleCallback ?? setTimeout)(() => {
      const s = document.createElement('script')
      s.src = 'https://widget.example.com/chat.js'
      s.async = true
      document.body.append(s)
    })
  }, [])
  // …
}
