cells.label: third-party
cells.bodyHtml: React Router-maintained adapters: @react-router/serve and @react-router/express (Node), @react-router/cloudflare, and @react-router/architect (AWS); v8 removed the Cloudflare dev proxy in favor of @cloudflare/vite-plugin. Vercel (@vercel/react-router preset) and Netlify (@netlify/vite-plugin-react-router) are host-maintained, not React Router-owned, so two of the four hosts this repo targets rely on host packages. (adapter, deploying, react-router, react-router, react-router)
cells.exampleHtml:
The port picks a host plugin from environment variables at build time. Cloudflare uses @cloudflare/vite-plugin, Netlify uses its own React Router plugin, and Vercel uses the vercelPreset() in react-router.config.ts.

// vite.config.ts
import { reactRouter } from '@react-router/dev/vite'
import { cloudflare } from '@cloudflare/vite-plugin'
import netlifyReactRouter from '@netlify/vite-plugin-react-router'
import { defineConfig, type PluginOption } from 'vite'

const env = process.env
const isCloudflare = !!(env.CLOUDFLARE || env.WORKERS_CI || env.CF_PAGES)
const isNetlify = !!env.NETLIFY && !isCloudflare

const hostPlugins: PluginOption[] = isCloudflare
  ? [cloudflare({ viteEnvironment: { name: 'ssr' } })]
  : isNetlify
    ? [netlifyReactRouter()]
    : []

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [...hostPlugins, reactRouter()],
})

Source: React Router: Deploying

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: No service worker support documented. The community @vite-pwa/remix package (0.2.0, published 2025-03-30) targets Remix and does not state React Router v8 support, so it is not credited. Hand-write the worker in public/ and register it. (vite-pwa remix)
cells.exampleHtml:
Put a hand-written worker in public/ and register it with an inline script in the root route.

// public/sw.js
const CACHE = 'books-v1'; // change the name on each deploy

self.addEventListener('activate', (event) => {
  event.waitUntil(
    caches.keys().then((keys) => Promise.all(keys.filter((k) => k !== CACHE).map((k) => caches.delete(k)))),
  );
});

self.addEventListener('fetch', (event) => {
  const { request } = event;
  if (request.method !== 'GET' || new URL(request.url).origin !== location.origin) return;
  // Network first, so pages stay current. The cached copy answers when offline.
  event.respondWith(
    fetch(request)
      .then((response) => {
        const copy = response.clone();
        caches.open(CACHE).then((cache) => cache.put(request, copy));
        return response;
      })
      .catch(() => caches.match(request)),
  );
});
// app/root.tsx
const swScript = `if('serviceWorker' in navigator)addEventListener('load',function(){navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js')});`;
// … in <head>
        <script dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: swScript }} />

Source: Using Service Workers (MDN)

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: A global stylesheet under 10KB is inlined automatically in production; larger files load separately. useStyles$ / useStylesScoped$ are lazy-loadable. (styles)

Import the global stylesheet in root.tsx. In production Qwik inlines it when it is under 10KB. Component styles registered with useStylesScoped$ load only with the component.

// src/root.tsx
import { component$ } from '@builder.io/qwik'
import { QwikCityProvider, RouterOutlet } from '@builder.io/qwik-city'
import { RouterHead } from './components/router-head/router-head'

import './styles/global.css' // inlined in production if < 10KB

export default component$(() => (
  <QwikCityProvider>
    <head><meta charset="utf-8" /><RouterHead /></head>
    <body><RouterOutlet /></body>
  </QwikCityProvider>
))
// src/components/card/card.tsx
import { component$, useStylesScoped$ } from '@builder.io/qwik'
import styles from './card.css?inline'

export const Card = component$(() => {
  useStylesScoped$(styles)
  return <div class="card">…</div>
})

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: cacheControl({ staleWhileRevalidate, maxAge, sMaxAge, public }) in onGet per layout/route. SSG via the static adapter; no data cache and no ISR documented. (caching, static-site-generation)
cells.exampleHtml:
Call cacheControl in a layout's or route's onGet to set the Cache-Control header for every page under it. A nested layout can override it.

// src/routes/layout.tsx
import type { RequestHandler } from '@builder.io/qwik-city'

export const onGet: RequestHandler = async ({ cacheControl }) => {
  cacheControl({
    public: true,
    maxAge: 5,
    sMaxAge: 10,
    staleWhileRevalidate: 60 * 60 * 24 * 365,
  })
}

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: <Link> prefetches on hover by default (prefetch={false} disables). The preloader adds <link rel="modulepreload"> for handlers and dependencies using a bundle graph; works only in preview/production builds. (routing, modules-prefetching, speculative-module-fetching)
cells.exampleHtml:
<Link> starts prefetching the next page when the user hovers it. Set prefetch={false} to turn that off for one link.

// src/components/nav/nav.tsx
import { component$ } from '@builder.io/qwik'
import { Link } from '@builder.io/qwik-city'

export const Nav = component$(() => (
  <nav>
    <Link href="/books">Books</Link>
    <Link href="/account" prefetch={false}>Account</Link>
  </nav>
))

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Return an async function from routeLoader$ and render it with <Resource>; Qwik streams the HTML up to that point and sends the rest when the function resolves. Streaming is in order, tuned by the streaming.inOrder render options. (streaming-deferred-loaders, qwik-server)
cells.exampleHtml:
Return an async function from routeLoader$ and render it with <Resource>. The HTML above the resource streams first, and the rest follows when the data resolves.

// src/routes/books/[id]/index.tsx
import { Resource, component$ } from '@builder.io/qwik'
import { routeLoader$ } from '@builder.io/qwik-city'

export const useReviews = routeLoader$(({ params }) => {
  // returning a function defers it: rendering doesn't wait here
  return async () => {
    const res = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/books/${params.id}/reviews`)
    return (await res.json()) as { id: string; text: string }[]
  }
})

export default component$(() => {
  const reviews = useReviews()
  return (
    <>
      <h1>Reviews</h1>
      <Resource
        value={reviews}
        onPending={() => <p>Loading…</p>}
        onResolved={(list) => <ul>{list.map((r) => <li key={r.id}>{r.text}</li>)}</ul>}
      />
    </>
  )
})

Source: Qwik: Streaming deferred loaders

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Resumability: no hydration step; state and listeners are serialized in HTML and handler chunks load lazily. The FAQ says Qwik does not use partial hydration (islands). qwikify$ (@builder.io/qwik-react) gives React islands with client:visible/client:idle. (resumable, faq, react)

Qwik components do not hydrate. The click handler below is serialized into the HTML and its code chunk loads on the first click. React components can still run as islands through qwikify$ with a client:* prop.

// src/components/counter/counter.tsx
import { component$, useSignal } from '@builder.io/qwik'

export const Counter = component$(() => {
  const count = useSignal(0)
  // no JS runs until the first click; then only this handler loads
  return <button onClick$={() => count.value++}>Increment {count.value}</button>
})
// src/integrations/react/slider.tsx
/** @jsxImportSource react */
import { qwikify$ } from '@builder.io/qwik-react'
import { Slider } from '@mui/material'

export const MUISlider = qwikify$(Slider)
// usage in a Qwik component: <MUISlider client:visible />

}

plugins: [

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Signals/stores re-run dependent components; the FAQ says Qwik uses the vDOM "only sometimes" and otherwise updates the DOM directly (non-structural changes). The scope is not detailed. (faq, state)
cells.exampleHtml:
useSignal and useStore are tracked. Changing a value updates the parts of the DOM that read it.

// src/components/counter/counter.tsx
import { component$, useSignal, useStore } from '@builder.io/qwik'

export const Counter = component$(() => {
  const count = useSignal(0)
  const state = useStore({ name: 'Qwik' })
  return (
    <>
      <button onClick$={() => count.value++}>Increment {count.value}</button>
      <input value={state.name} onInput$={(_, el) => (state.name = el.value)} />
    </>
  )
})

cells.bodyHtml: qwik add adapters: Node (express, fastify), vercel-edge, netlify-edge, cloudflare-pages, cloudflare-workers. (deployments, node, vercel-edge, netlify-edge, cloudflare-pages, cloudflare-workers)
cells.exampleHtml:
qwik add express (or vercel-edge, netlify-edge, cloudflare-pages) writes an adapter config that extends the base Vite config. The Books port keeps one per host under adapters/.

cells.label: third-party
cells.bodyHtml: optimization.fonts.inline (default true) inlines external Google Fonts and Adobe Fonts CSS into the index HTML (needs internet at build). That removes one render-blocking stylesheet request, but the font files still load from the font host; no self-hosting, subsetting, or preload is documented. Self-hosting needs a package such as Fontsource, as for React Router, Qwik City, Marko, and Fresh. Our feature test confirmed this: with fonts.inline on, the Google CSS was inlined and the font file was still fetched from fonts.gstatic.com. (workspace-config, Fontsource)
cells.exampleHtml:
Link a Google Fonts stylesheet in index.html as usual. With optimization.fonts.inline on, the production build downloads that CSS and inlines it into the HTML, removing one render-blocking request.

<!-- src/index.html -->
<head>
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin />
  <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;600&display=swap" rel="stylesheet" />
</head>
// angular.json (production configuration; needs internet access at build time)
"optimization": {
  "fonts": { "inline": true }

cells.bodyHtml: NgOptimizedImage: priority (fetchpriority=high, eager, SSR preload link), auto srcset, placeholder blur, lazy by default. Built-in loaders for Cloudflare Image Resizing, Cloudinary, ImageKit, Imgix, Netlify; it does not resize itself (the default loader is a no-op). (image-optimization)

// src/app/app.config.ts
import { provideImgixLoader } from '@angular/common';

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [provideImgixLoader('https://books.imgix.net/')],
};

// src/app/book/book-cover.ts
import { NgOptimizedImage } from '@angular/common';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-book-cover',
  imports: [NgOptimizedImage],
  template: `
    <img [ngSrc]="src()" width="400" height="600" [alt]="title()"
         ngSrcset="200w, 400w, 800w" sizes="(max-width: 640px) 50vw, 200px"
         [priority]="priority()" placeholder />
  `,
})
export class BookCover { /* … */ }

artDirection.label: manual
artDirection.bodyHtml: The NgOptimizedImage page says <picture> is not supported yet ("on our roadmap"); no art direction or <source type> format fallback is documented. Format is left to the configured image-CDN loader (the page says only that the loader sets "size, format, and image quality transformations"). No first-party <picture> documented; hand-write it. (image-optimization)
artDirection.exampleHtml:
NgOptimizedImage can't render <picture>, so write the element in a component template with plain <source> tags for format fallback and art direction.

// src/app/home/hero-image.ts
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component } from '@angular/core';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-hero-image',
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  template: `
    <picture>
      <!-- art direction: a square crop on narrow screens -->
      <source media="(max-width: 640px)" type="image/avif"
              srcset="/media/hero-square-640.avif" width="640" height="640" />
      <!-- format fallback: AVIF, then WebP, then the <img> JPEG -->
      <source type="image/avif" sizes="100vw"
              srcset="/media/hero-1280.avif 1280w, /media/hero-1920.avif 1920w" />
      <source type="image/webp" sizes="100vw"
              srcset="/media/hero-1280.webp 1280w, /media/hero-1920.webp 1920w" />
      <img src="/media/hero-1280.jpg" alt="Shelves of books" width="1280" height="720"
           fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" />
    </picture>
  `,
})
export class HeroImage {}

cells.bodyHtml: RenderMode.Prerender build-time HTML; the HttpClient transfer cache (withHttpTransferCacheOptions) reuses SSR responses on hydration; per-route headers. No ISR/revalidate or server data cache documented. (ssr, withHttpTransferCacheOptions)
cells.exampleHtml:
Prerender stable pages at build time, and let the HttpClient transfer cache hand SSR responses to the browser so hydration does not fetch them again.

// src/app/app.routes.server.ts
export const serverRoutes: ServerRoute[] = [
  { path: 'about', renderMode: RenderMode.Prerender },
  { path: '**', renderMode: RenderMode.Server, headers: { 'Cache-Control': 'public, max-age=60' } },
];

// src/app/app.config.ts
import { provideClientHydration, withHttpTransferCacheOptions } from '@angular/platform-browser';

providers: [
  provideClientHydration(
    withHttpTransferCacheOptions({
      includeHeaders: ['ETag', 'Cache-Control'],
      filter: (req) => !req.url.includes('/api/profile'),
      includePostRequests: false,
    }),
  ),
],

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Opt-in withPreloading(PreloadAllModules) preloads lazy route chunks; @defer has prefetch on idle/viewport/hover. No link hover/viewport prefetch documented. The default strategy is NoPreloading, so nothing is preloaded until withPreloading(...) is added. (NoPreloading, PreloadAllModules, defer)
cells.exampleHtml:
The router preloads nothing by default (NoPreloading). Add withPreloading(PreloadAllModules) to fetch every lazy route chunk after the app starts. @defer blocks take their own prefetch trigger.

// src/app/app.config.ts
import { ApplicationConfig } from '@angular/core';
import { provideRouter, withPreloading, PreloadAllModules } from '@angular/router';
import { routes } from './app.routes';

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [provideRouter(routes, withPreloading(PreloadAllModules))],
};
<!-- any template: load the chunk on interaction, prefetch it when the browser is idle -->
@defer (on interaction; prefetch on idle) {
  <app-book-reviews />
} @placeholder {
  <button>Show reviews</button>
}

Source: Angular: Customizing route behavior

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: No streaming render documented. The SSR guide describes rendering the page to a complete HTML document and then sending it, and the word "stream" does not appear in it. (ssr)
cells.exampleHtml:
Angular renders the whole document before sending it. To get bytes out sooner, flush a fixed <head> from the Express handler while Angular renders, then send the rest of Angular's HTML. The status code and head are fixed before rendering starts.

// src/server.ts
import { AngularNodeAppEngine } from '@angular/ssr/node';
import express from 'express';

const app = express();
const angularApp = new AngularNodeAppEngine();
// Copy the <head> of the built index.server.html, with its hashed CSS link.
const HEAD = `<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Books</title>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/styles-HASH.css"></head>`;

app.use(async (req, res, next) => {
  if (!req.accepts('html')) return next();
  res.status(200).type('html').write(HEAD); // sent before Angular renders
  const response = await angularApp.handle(req);
  const html = response ? await response.text() : '<body></body>';
  res.end(html.slice(html.indexOf('</head>') + '</head>'.length)); // body only
});

Source: Angular: Server-side rendering

cells.bodyHtml: No first-party preload Link headers or 103 Early Hints documented. Per-route headers in ServerRoute and RESPONSE_INIT can set a Link header by hand. (ssr)
cells.exampleHtml:
Add a Link header to the server route's headers. This one preconnects to the font host. To preload a built file with a hashed name, read its URL from the Vite manifest.

// src/app/app.routes.server.ts
import { RenderMode, ServerRoute } from '@angular/ssr';

export const serverRoutes: ServerRoute[] = [
  {
    path: '**',
    renderMode: RenderMode.Server,
    headers: { Link: '<https://fonts.gstatic.com>; rel=preconnect; crossorigin' },
  },
];

cells.bodyHtml: Incremental hydration via @defer with hydrate on idle/viewport/interaction/hover/immediate/timer/when and hydrate never; the v22 guide says it is enabled by default with provideClientHydration(). Stable since v20 per the roadmap (developer preview in v19), and on by default since v22.0.0, when withIncrementalHydration was deprecated (withIncrementalHydration); the v22 guide pages carry no stability label. (incremental-hydration, hydration)
cells.exampleHtml:
Incremental hydration is on by default with provideClientHydration(). A @defer block with a hydrate trigger renders on the server and stays dehydrated until the trigger fires.

// src/app/app.config.ts
providers: [provideClientHydration()],
<!-- src/app/pages/book.page.ts template -->
<app-book-detail [book]="book()" />

@defer (hydrate on viewport) {
  <app-related-books [bookId]="book().id" />
}

@defer (on viewport; hydrate never) {
  <app-static-footer />
}

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: ServerRoute[] in app.routes.server.ts with RenderMode.Server/Client/Prerender; getPrerenderParams, fallback, per-route headers/status; outputMode: "static" for server-less builds. Stable since v20 per the roadmap (developer preview in v19); the guide itself carries no stability label. (ssr)
cells.exampleHtml:
Each route picks a render mode in app.routes.server.ts: per-request SSR, build-time prerender, or client-only.

// src/app/app.routes.server.ts
import { inject } from '@angular/core';
import { RenderMode, PrerenderFallback, ServerRoute } from '@angular/ssr';

export const serverRoutes: ServerRoute[] = [
  { path: '', renderMode: RenderMode.Server },
  { path: 'about', renderMode: RenderMode.Prerender },
  { path: 'account', renderMode: RenderMode.Client },
  {
    path: 'book/:id',
    renderMode: RenderMode.Prerender,
    fallback: PrerenderFallback.Server,
    async getPrerenderParams() {
      const ids = await inject(BooksApi).topIds();
      return ids.map((id) => ({ id }));
    },
  },
  { path: '**', renderMode: RenderMode.Server, status: 404 },
];

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Signals (signal, computed, linkedSignal, effect, resource) track dependencies dynamically; zoneless is default from v21. The page gives no stability label. (signals, zoneless)
cells.exampleHtml:
From the Books port's cover component: input() and signal() hold state, computed() derives from them, and the template re-renders only what reads a changed signal.

// src/app/book/book-cover.ts
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, computed, input, signal } from '@angular/core';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-book-cover',
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  template: `
    @if (showImage()) {
      <img [src]="readySrc()" [alt]="title()" (error)="failedSrc.set(readySrc())" />
    } @else {
      <div role="img">Cover unavailable</div>
    }
  `,
})
export class BookCover {
  readonly title = input.required<string>();
  readonly src = input.required<string | null>();
  protected readonly failedSrc = signal<string | null>(null);
  protected readonly readySrc = computed(() => getLargeBookImageUrl(this.src() ?? EMPTY_IMAGE_URL));
  protected readonly showImage = computed(() => this.readySrc() !== this.failedSrc());
}

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: No first-party script-loading primitive documented (the runtime-performance page lists none). Rests on absence. (runtime-performance)
cells.exampleHtml:
Put the loading strategy in the tag yourself: async in src/index.html for early scripts, or afterNextRender to inject one after the first browser render.

// src/index.html: loads in parallel, runs as soon as it arrives
// <script async src="https://plausible.io/js/script.js" data-domain="books.example"></script>

// src/app/app.ts: load a chat widget only in the browser, after first render
import { Component, afterNextRender } from '@angular/core';

@Component({ selector: 'app-root', templateUrl: './app.html' })
export class App {
  constructor() {
    afterNextRender(() => {
      // Never runs during SSR; wait for idle so the widget doesn't compete with hydration.
      (window.requestIdleCallback ?? setTimeout)(() => {
        const s = document.createElement('script');
        s.src = 'https://widget.example.com/chat.js';
        s.async = true;
        document.body.append(s);
      });
    });
  }
}

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: Web-standard AngularAppEngine / createRequestHandler is portable, with AngularNodeAppEngine for Node and outputMode: "static". SSR is documented for Node (first-party), Netlify (host-maintained @netlify/angular-runtime, Edge Function) and Cloudflare Workers: the Cloudflare guide scaffolds an SSR Worker through create-cloudflare --framework=angular (AngularAppEngine, ssr.platform: "neutral"), maintained by Cloudflare rather than the Angular team, though the guide page itself does not mention SSR and its automatic-configuration example is assets-only. Vercel lists Angular only as a zero-config frontend framework and no Vercel Angular SSR page was found, so the four hosts this repo targets are not all covered. The deployment page also lists third-party ng deploy builders. This portability judgment is lower confidence. (ssr, angular, angular, frontend, deployment)
cells.exampleHtml:
From the port: one AngularAppEngine handler per host, each picked by a build configuration in angular.json. Vercel reuses the Node/Express build behind a function.

// angular-books/src/server.cloudflare.ts (Netlify's server.netlify.ts is the same shape)
import { AngularAppEngine, createRequestHandler } from '@angular/ssr';
// …
const angularAppEngine = new AngularAppEngine();

async function handle(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
  const result = await angularAppEngine.handle(request);
  return result || new Response('Not found', { status: 404 });
}

export const reqHandler = createRequestHandler(handle);
export default { fetch: (request: Request) => handle(request) };

// angular-books/angular.json, build.configurations: one SSR entry per host
// "node":       { "ssr": { "entry": "src/server.ts" } },
// "cloudflare": { "ssr": { "entry": "src/server.cloudflare.ts", "platform": "neutral" } },
// "netlify":    {}  // default "ssr.entry": "src/server.netlify.ts"

// angular-books/api/index.js: Vercel function wrapping the Express build
// handler ??= (await import('../dist/angular-books/server/server.mjs')).reqHandler;

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: ng add @angular/pwa adds @angular/service-worker, registers it, and creates ngsw-config.json; the build writes the hashed asset manifest, and the worker caches the app shell and configured data groups. (getting-started, service-workers)
cells.exampleHtml:
ng add @angular/pwa adds @angular/service-worker, registers it in the app config and creates ngsw-config.json. The build writes the asset manifest the worker uses.

// src/app/app.config.ts
import { ApplicationConfig, isDevMode } from '@angular/core';
import { provideServiceWorker } from '@angular/service-worker';

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideServiceWorker('ngsw-worker.js', {
      enabled: !isDevMode(),
      registrationStrategy: 'registerWhenStable:30000',
    }),
  ],
};
// ngsw-config.json
{
  "index": "/index.html",
  "assetGroups": [
    { "name": "app", "installMode": "prefetch",
      "resources": { "files": ["/favicon.ico", "/index.html", "/*.css", "/*.js"] } }
  ],
  "dataGroups": [
    { "name": "api", "urls": ["/api/**"],
      "cacheConfig": { "strategy": "performance", "maxSize": 100, "maxAge": "1d" } }
  ]
}

cells.label: third-party
cells.bodyHtml: No image component or optimizer documented; the native-tag page and the full reference contain only an og:image meta example and plain <img>. @marko/vite rewrites static relative <img src> paths to hashed Vite assets but does not resize or convert. A host image CDN wired by hand is the third-party route, as for React Router and Ember. (native-tag)
cells.exampleHtml:
Marko has no image component, so a small tag builds a srcset against the host's image CDN. This one uses Netlify Image CDN URLs; remote sources must be allowlisted in netlify.toml.

// src/tags/book-cover.marko
export interface Input { src: string; title: string; sizes: string; priority?: boolean }

static const WIDTHS = [160, 320, 640];
static function cdn(src: string, w: number) {
  return `/.netlify/images?url=${encodeURIComponent(src)}&w=${w}&q=75`;
}

<img
  src=cdn(input.src, 320)
  srcset=WIDTHS.map((w) => `${cdn(input.src, w)} ${w}w`).join(", ")
  sizes=input.sizes
  alt=input.title
  width=320 height=480
  loading=(input.priority ? "eager" : "lazy")
  fetchpriority=(input.priority ? "high" : undefined)
/>
# netlify.toml
[images]
  remote_images = ['https://images\.gr-assets\.com/.*']

// src/tags/hero-image.marko
export interface Input {
  alt: string;
  priority?: boolean;
}

<picture>
  <source media="(min-width: 1000px)" type="image/avif" srcset="/hero-wide.avif">
  <source media="(min-width: 1000px)" srcset="/hero-wide.jpg">
  <source type="image/avif" srcset="/hero-tall.avif">
  <img
    src="/hero-tall.jpg"
    alt=input.alt
    width=750
    height=1334
    decoding="async"
    fetchpriority=(input.priority ? "high" : undefined)
    loading=(input.priority ? "eager" : "lazy")

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: Marko Run documents no data cache, ISR, or cache-header API. @marko/run-adapter-static builds the whole app into static files by crawling relative links (urls option for extras), with no revalidation and no per-route choice, so it does not cache a server-rendered app. Otherwise the app hand-sets Cache-Control on web-standard Request/Response, the same basis as Fresh. Our feature test passed only by setting Cache-Control by hand in the route's GET handler. (adapters)
cells.exampleHtml:
For a fully static site, swap in @marko/run-adapter-static, which crawls links at build time; urls adds pages the crawler can't reach. For server-rendered pages, set Cache-Control yourself in middleware, as the Books port does.

// vite.config.ts (static build)
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import marko from "@marko/run/vite";
import staticAdapter from "@marko/run-adapter-static";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [marko({ adapter: staticAdapter({ urls: ["/about", "/1"] }) })],
});
// src/routes/+middleware.ts (server build)
export default async (_ctx: unknown, next: () => Promise<Response>) => {
  const response = await next();
  if (!response.headers.get("content-type")?.includes("text/html")) return response;
  const headers = new Headers(response.headers);
  headers.set("Cache-Control", "public, max-age=0, must-revalidate");
  return new Response(response.body, { status: response.status, headers });
};

Source: Marko Run: Adapters

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: No prefetch/preload API in the Marko Run docs or full reference. Lazy load triggers (visible, idle, media, events) defer a tag's JS only; that is not route prefetch. (lazy-loading)
cells.exampleHtml:
Marko Run navigates with full documents, so a Speculation Rules block in the layout handles it. Supporting browsers prefetch same-origin links on hover; the others ignore the block.

// src/routes/+layout.marko
<head>
  // …
  <html-script type="speculationrules">
    {
      "prefetch": [{
        "where": { "and": [
          { "href_matches": "/*" },
          { "not": { "selector_matches": "[rel~=nofollow]" } }
        ]},
        "eagerness": "moderate"
      }]
    }
  </html-script>
</head>

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Streaming is the default. Marko flushes HTML up to each <await> and sends the rest when its promise resolves; a <try> with @placeholder opts into out-of-order streaming and shows the placeholder first. (streaming)
cells.exampleHtml:
The handler passes the queries to the page as unresolved promises. Each <await> sits in a <try> with @placeholder, so the skeleton is sent first and the grid streams in when its promise resolves.

// src/routes/+handler.ts
export const GET = Run.GET((ctx, next) => {
  const params = parseSearchParams(ctx.search ?? {});
  return next({
    books: loadBooksPage(params),   // not awaited
    count: loadBooksCount(params),  // not awaited
  });
});
// src/routes/+page.marko
<try>
  <await|books|=$global.data.books>
    <book-grid books=books/>
  </await>
  <@placeholder><book-grid-skeleton/></@placeholder>
  <@catch|err|><error-state title="Can't load books" body=err.message/></@catch>
</try>

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: No first-party preload Link headers or 103 Early Hints documented. Handlers return web-standard Response objects, so a Link header is set by hand in a +handler or +middleware file. (file-based-routing)
cells.exampleHtml:
Set a Link header on HTML responses in the root middleware. This one preconnects to the font host. To preload a built file with a hashed name, read its URL from the Vite manifest.

// src/routes/+middleware.ts
const LINK = '<https://fonts.gstatic.com>; rel=preconnect; crossorigin';

export default async (_ctx: unknown, next: () => Promise<Response>) => {
  const response = await next();
  if (response.headers.get('content-type')?.includes('text/html')) response.headers.append('Link', LINK);
  return response;

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: Marko Run documents streaming SSR; the static adapter is app-wide and +meta.* is static metadata only. No per-route render-mode switch documented. (file-based-routing, adapters)
cells.exampleHtml:
Every route still streams SSR. You tag a route with a mode in +meta.json, and the root middleware turns it into CDN Cache-Control. This adapts the port's +middleware.ts.

// src/routes/about/+meta.json   →  { "render": "static" }
// src/routes/+meta.json         →  { "render": "isr" }

// src/routes/+middleware.ts
const cacheControl: Record<string, string> = {
  static: "public, s-maxage=31536000",                // cached until redeploy
  isr: "public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=86400",
};

export default Run.ALL(async (ctx, next) => {
  const res = await next();
  if (!res.headers.get("content-type")?.includes("text/html")) return res;
  const mode = (ctx.meta as { render?: string } | undefined)?.render;
  const headers = new Headers(res.headers);
  headers.set("Cache-Control", cacheControl[mode ?? ""] ?? "private, no-store"); // SSR
  return new Response(res.body, { status: res.status, statusText: res.statusText, headers });
});

Marko's <script> is a mount effect, so you use <html-script> for a literal async tag. A <script> effect then loads the low-priority widget at browser idle.

// src/routes/+layout.marko
<head>
  // …
  // literal tag in the HTML: downloads in parallel, never blocks parsing
  <html-script async src="https://analytics.example.com/script.js"></html-script>
</head>
<body>
  <${input.content}/>
  // runs once in the browser after mount, then waits for idle

    (window.requestIdleCallback || setTimeout)(() => {
      const s = document.createElement("script");
      s.src = "https://widget.example.com/chat.js";
      s.async = true;
      document.head.append(s);

cells.bodyHtml: Official adapters for Node, Static and Netlify (Functions or Edge, needs netlify.toml) are on the adapters page. Cloudflare Workers (@marko/run-adapter-cloudflare) is announced as an official adapter in the markojs.com October 2026 newsletter but is not yet on the adapters page. @marko/run-adapter-vercel (npm 0.1.1) is published from the marko-js/run repository by the same maintainers as @marko/run and is documented only in its repo README, not on markojs.com. The Books port picks an adapter at build time from an env var. The default Node adapter covers local and container runs; the Netlify, Vercel and Cloudflare adapters build for each host.

// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import marko from "@marko/run/vite";

export default defineConfig(async () => {
  const adapter = process.env.CLOUDFLARE
    ? (await import("@marko/run-adapter-cloudflare")).default()
    : process.env.NETLIFY
      ? (await import("@marko/run-adapter-netlify")).default() // { edge: true } for Edge Functions
      : process.env.VERCEL
        ? (await import("@marko/run-adapter-vercel")).default()
        : (await import("@marko/run/adapter")).default();

  return { plugins: [marko({ adapter })] };
});

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: No service worker support documented in the Marko or Marko Run docs. Hand-write the worker, serve it as a static file, and register it from a <script>. (file-based-routing)
cells.exampleHtml:
Put a hand-written worker in public/ and register it with an inline script in the root layout.

// public/sw.js
const CACHE = 'books-v1'; // change the name on each deploy

self.addEventListener('activate', (event) => {
  event.waitUntil(
    caches.keys().then((keys) => Promise.all(keys.filter((k) => k !== CACHE).map((k) => caches.delete(k)))),
  );
});

self.addEventListener('fetch', (event) => {
  const { request } = event;
  if (request.method !== 'GET' || new URL(request.url).origin !== location.origin) return;
  // Network first, so pages stay current. The cached copy answers when offline.
  event.respondWith(
    fetch(request)
      .then((response) => {
        const copy = response.clone();
        caches.open(CACHE).then((cache) => cache.put(request, copy));
        return response;
      })
      .catch(() => caches.match(request)),
  );
});
// src/routes/+layout.marko
static const SW_SCRIPT = `if('serviceWorker' in navigator)addEventListener('load',function(){navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js')});`;
// … in <head>
    <html-script>$!{SW_SCRIPT}</html-script>

cells.bodyHtml: No first-party cache documented; set Cache-Control by hand via page(data, { headers }). Build-time prerender exists only as an open, unmerged PR, not in the docs and not credited. (data-fetching, 3766)
cells.exampleHtml:
You wrap each query in a TTL cache backed by a host store, and set the HTML Cache-Control in app middleware. This comes from the port.

// lib/catalog-cache.server.ts
export function withTtlCache<Args extends unknown[], Result>(
  name: string,
  fn: (...args: Args) => Promise<Result>,
): (...args: Args) => Promise<Result> {
  // in-memory Map → Workers KV / Vercel getCache / Netlify Blobs → fn()
  return (...args: Args) => cacheLifeHours(`${name}:${JSON.stringify(args)}`, () => fn(...args))
}

// features/book/book-queries.server.ts
export const getBooksPage = withTtlCache('getBooksPage', getBooksPageUncached)

// main.ts
app.use(async (ctx) => {
  const res = await ctx.next();
  if (!res.headers.get("content-type")?.includes("text/html")) return res;
  const headers = new Headers(res.headers);
  headers.set("Cache-Control", hostDocumentCacheControl());
  return new Response(res.body, { status: res.status, statusText: res.statusText, headers });
});

cells.exampleHtml:
Add a Speculation Rules block to _app.tsx. Supporting browsers prefetch same-origin pages on hover, and other browsers ignore it. The prefetch only helps full-page navigations, so it does not speed up links that use Fresh partials (f-client-nav).

// routes/_app.tsx
const speculationRules = JSON.stringify({
  prefetch: [{
    where: { and: [
      { href_matches: "/*" },
      { not: { selector_matches: "[rel~=nofollow]" } },
    ] },
    eagerness: "moderate",

});

<script type="speculationrules" dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: speculationRules }} />

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: No streamed page rendering documented. The docs show a ReadableStream returned from an API handler only, and describe no way to flush part of a page early. (common-patterns, data-fetching)
cells.exampleHtml:
Write the route handler yourself and return a ReadableStream of HTML. The shell and a placeholder go out first. When the query resolves, the handler sends the rendered grid and a small script that swaps it in. This page skips Fresh's layouts and islands.

// routes/books.tsx
import { define } from "@/utils.ts";
import { renderToString } from "preact-render-to-string";

export const handler = define.handlers({
  GET() {
    const enc = new TextEncoder();
    const body = new ReadableStream({
      async start(controller) {
        controller.enqueue(enc.encode(
          `<!doctype html><html><head><link rel="stylesheet" href="/styles.css"></head>` +
          `<body><main id="grid">Loading…</main>`,
        ));
        const books = await getBooks();
        controller.enqueue(enc.encode(
          `<template id="grid-html">${renderToString(<BookGrid books={books} />)}</template>` +
          `<script>document.getElementById("grid").replaceWith(document.getElementById("grid-html").content)</script></body></html>`,
        ));
        controller.close();
      },
    });
    return new Response(body, { headers: { "Content-Type": "text/html; charset=utf-8" } });
  },
});

import MobileSidebar from '@/islands/MobileSidebar.tsx';
import MobileSidebarTrigger from '@/islands/MobileSidebarTrigger.tsx';

export default define.layout(function Layout({ Component, url }) {

    <>

        {/* server-rendered children passed into an island */}
        <BookSidebar current={current} idPrefix="mobile" mobile />
      </MobileSidebar>
      <header>
        <MobileSidebarTrigger />
        <BookSearch current={current} />
      </header>
      <main><Component /></main>
    </>
  );
});

// main.ts
const modes: Record<string, string> = {
  "/about": "public, s-maxage=31536000",                    // "static": cached until redeploy
  "/": "public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=86400", // "ISR": revalidate each minute

app.use(async (ctx) => {

  if (!res.headers.get("content-type")?.includes("text/html")) return res;

  headers.set("Cache-Control", modes[ctx.url.pathname] ?? "private, no-store"); // SSR

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: analog({ prerender: { routes } }) renders listed routes to static HTML at build time, static: true builds a server-less site, and prerendered server-side data is written as static files. Response headers are set with h3 setResponseHeader in middleware or API routes. No ISR or revalidate option documented. (static-site-generation, middleware)
cells.exampleHtml:
List routes under prerender.routes to build them as static HTML. Set staticData: true on a route to write its server-side data to static files too. Dynamic responses get headers from server middleware.

// vite.config.ts
import analog from '@analogjs/platform';
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';

export default defineConfig(() => ({
  plugins: [
    analog({
      prerender: {
        routes: async () => ['/', '/about', { route: '/books', staticData: true }],
      },
    }),
  ],
}));
// src/server/middleware/cache.ts
import { defineEventHandler, setResponseHeader } from 'h3';

export default defineEventHandler((event) => {
  if (event.path.startsWith('/books/')) {
    setResponseHeader(event, 'Cache-Control', 'public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=300');
  }
});

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Angular Router preloading: pass withPreloading(PreloadAllModules) to provideFileRouter(...), which accepts Angular router features, to preload lazy route chunks. The Analog docs show other router features there (withComponentInputBinding, withNavigationErrorHandler) and no preloading example. No link hover or viewport prefetch documented. (routing, PreloadAllModules)

provideFileRouter() takes Angular router features. withPreloading(PreloadAllModules) loads every lazy page chunk after the app starts.

// src/app/app.config.ts
import { ApplicationConfig } from '@angular/core';
import { provideFileRouter } from '@analogjs/router';
import { PreloadAllModules, withComponentInputBinding, withPreloading } from '@angular/router';

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideFileRouter(withComponentInputBinding(), withPreloading(PreloadAllModules)),
    // …

};

The default SSR path stays buffered. (streaming-ssr)

// vite.config.ts
import analog from '@analogjs/platform';
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [analog({ experimental: { streaming: true } })],
});

// src/main.server.ts
import { renderStream } from '@analogjs/router/server';
import { config } from './app/app.config.server';
import { AppComponent } from './app/app.component';

export default renderStream(AppComponent, config);

// src/server/middleware/preload.ts
import { defineEventHandler, setResponseHeader } from 'h3';

export default defineEventHandler((event) => {
  if (event.path.startsWith('/api')) return;
  setResponseHeader(
    event,
    'Link',
    '<https://fonts.gstatic.com>; rel=preconnect; crossorigin, </media/hero-1280.avif>; rel=preload; as=image',

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Angular incremental hydration: @defer (hydrate on viewport | idle | interaction | immediate) blocks, enabled with provideClientHydration(withIncrementalHydration()) on Angular 21 and by default on Angular 22. Analog's streaming SSR page builds on it; streaming itself is experimental (experimental.streaming). (streaming-ssr, incremental-hydration)
cells.exampleHtml:
Enable incremental hydration, then wrap a part of the page in @defer with a hydrate trigger. It renders on the server and hydrates when it scrolls into view.

// src/app/app.config.ts (Angular 21; on by default with provideClientHydration() from Angular 22)
import { provideClientHydration, withIncrementalHydration } from '@angular/platform-browser';
// providers: [provideClientHydration(withIncrementalHydration()), /* … */]

// src/app/pages/books/[id].page.ts
import { Component, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { Reviews } from '../../reviews/reviews';

@Component({
  imports: [Reviews],
  template: `
    <h1>{{ title() }}</h1>
    @defer (hydrate on viewport) {
      <app-reviews />
    } @placeholder {
      <div>Reviews</div>
    }
  `,
})
export default class BookPage {
  protected title = signal('Dune');
}

cells.bodyHtml: SSR is the default; routeRules: { '/admin/**': { ssr: false } } in the Nitro config renders matching routes on the client only, and prerender.routes lists the routes built as static HTML. (server-side-rendering, static-site-generation)

Pages render on the server by default. routeRules in the Nitro plugin makes matching routes client-only, and prerender.routes builds the listed routes as static HTML.

// vite.config.ts
import analog from '@analogjs/platform';
import angular from '@analogjs/vite-plugin-angular';
import nitro from '@analogjs/vite-plugin-nitro';
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';

export default defineConfig(() => ({
  plugins: [
    analog({ prerender: { routes: ['/', '/about'] } }), // static HTML
    angular(),
    nitro({
      routeRules: {
        '/admin/**': { ssr: false }, // client-only
      },
    }),
  ],
}));

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Angular signals (signal, computed, resource); Analog's own injectServerFn returns an Angular resource that refetches when a signal it reads changes. Zoneless change detection is the default from Angular 21. (server-functions, signals)
cells.exampleHtml:
A signal holds the search text. injectServerFn returns an Angular resource that refetches when a signal read in its args factory changes.

// src/app/pages/search.page.ts
import { Component, computed, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { injectServerFn } from '@analogjs/router';
import { searchBooks } from '../server-fns/books.server';

@Component({
  template: `
    <input [value]="query()" (input)="query.set($any($event.target).value)" />
    <p>{{ count() }} results</p>
    @for (book of books.value() ?? []; track book.id) {
      <p>{{ book.title }}</p>
    }
  `,
})
export default class SearchPage {
  query = signal('');
  protected books = injectServerFn(searchBooks, () => ({ q: this.query() }));
  count = computed(() => this.books.value()?.length ?? 0);
}

Write the loading strategy yourself: async in index.html for early scripts, or afterNextRender to inject one in the browser after the first render.

// index.html: loads in parallel, runs as soon as it arrives
// <script async src="https://plausible.io/js/script.js" data-domain="books.example"></script>

// src/app/app.component.ts: load a chat widget only in the browser
import { Component, afterNextRender } from '@angular/core';
import { RouterOutlet } from '@angular/router';

@Component({ selector: 'app-root', imports: [RouterOutlet], template: '<router-outlet />' })
export class AppComponent {
  constructor() {
    afterNextRender(() => {
      const s = document.createElement('script');
      s.src = 'https://widget.example.com/chat.js';
      s.async = true;
      document.body.append(s);
    });
  }
}

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: No service worker support documented in the Analog docs. Angular's ng add @angular/pwa "enables service worker build support in the CLI", and Analog replaces the Angular CLI build with Vite, so the ngsw.json asset manifest is not generated for you. Hand-write the worker and register it. (angular service workers, migrating)
cells.exampleHtml:
Put a hand-written worker in public/ and register it with an inline script in index.html.

// public/sw.js
const CACHE = 'books-v1'; // change the name on each deploy

self.addEventListener('activate', (event) => {
  event.waitUntil(
    caches.keys().then((keys) => Promise.all(keys.filter((k) => k !== CACHE).map((k) => caches.delete(k)))),
  );
});

self.addEventListener('fetch', (event) => {
  const { request } = event;
  if (request.method !== 'GET' || new URL(request.url).origin !== location.origin) return;
  // Network first, so pages stay current. The cached copy answers when offline.
  event.respondWith(
    fetch(request)
      .then((response) => {
        const copy = response.clone();
        caches.open(CACHE).then((cache) => cache.put(request, copy));
        return response;
      })
      .catch(() => caches.match(request)),
  );
});
<!-- index.html, before </head> -->
<script>
  if ('serviceWorker' in navigator) {
    addEventListener('load', () => navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js'));
  }
</script>

Source: Using Service Workers (MDN)

cells.bodyHtml: No first-party CSS inlining documented; Vike injects <link rel="stylesheet"> tags for a page's CSS. injectFilter() only moves or drops injected tags. Inline by hand, for example with a Vite ?inline import. (preloading)

// pages/+Head.tsx

export function Head() {

Use <Image> from @unpic/react. It builds a srcset for the image CDN that serves the URL and sets width, height and lazy loading.

// pages/book/@id/+Page.tsx
import { Image } from '@unpic/react'
import { useData } from 'vike-react/useData'

export function Page() {
  const book = useData<{ title: string; coverUrl: string }>()
  return (
    <Image src={book.coverUrl} layout="constrained" width={400} height={600} alt={book.title} priority />

}

artDirection.bodyHtml: No first-party <picture> helper documented; hand-write the markup. (image)
artDirection.exampleHtml:
Vike has no image component, so write <picture> in the page. With @unpic/react, each <Source> gets a media query and its own crop, and <Image> is the fallback.

// pages/book/@id/BookCover.tsx
import { Image, Source } from '@unpic/react'

export function BookCover({ title, coverUrl, wideUrl }: { title: string; coverUrl: string; wideUrl: string }) {
  return (
    <picture>
      {/* art direction: a wide banner crop on large screens */}
      <Source media="(min-width: 768px)" src={wideUrl} layout="constrained" width={1200} height={400} />
      <Image src={coverUrl} alt={title} layout="constrained" width={400} height={600} priority />
    </picture>
  )
}

cells.bodyHtml: prerender: true renders pages to static HTML at build time, per page or for the whole app. +headersResponse sets response headers such as Cache-Control per page; it is marked beta. On Vercel, vercel: { isr: { expiration: 30 } } in a page's +config.js opts into ISR through vite-plugin-vercel. No data cache documented. (pre-rendering, headersResponse, vercel)
cells.exampleHtml:
prerender: true builds pages to HTML. A dynamic page sets Cache-Control with +headersResponse. On Vercel, a page's +config can opt into ISR.

// pages/+config.ts
export default { prerender: true }

// pages/search/+config.ts
export default { prerender: false }

// pages/search/+headersResponse.ts
export function headersResponse() {
  return { 'Cache-Control': 'public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=600' }
}

// pages/book/@id/+config.ts (Vercel only, with vite-plugin-vercel)
export default { vercel: { isr: { expiration: 30 } } }

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: prefetchStaticAssets: 'hover' | 'viewport' | false, default 'hover', per page, with a per-link data-prefetch-static-assets override and a programmatic prefetch('/url'). Only static assets are prefetched; page data is not. (prefetchStaticAssets, prefetch)
cells.exampleHtml:
prefetchStaticAssets sets when a link's page assets are prefetched. A link can override it with data-prefetch-static-assets, and prefetch() starts it from code.

// pages/+config.ts
export default { prefetchStaticAssets: 'viewport' }

// components/BookLink.tsx
import { prefetch } from 'vike/client/router'

export function BookLink({ id }: { id: string }) {
  return (
    <a href={`/book/${id}`} data-prefetch-static-assets="hover" onFocus={() => prefetch(`/book/${id}`)}>
      Details
    </a>
  )
}

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Set stream: true in a +config.js, for the whole app or per page; it needs ssr: true and one of vike-react, vike-vue or vike-solid. The default is false. The deferred parts are the UI framework's own async boundaries: vike-react streams through react-streaming, and vike-react-query's useSuspenseQuery() shows a <Suspense> fallback while the rest of the page renders. (stream, streaming, vike-react-query)
cells.exampleHtml:
Set stream: true in +config. With vike-react-query, a component that calls useSuspenseQuery() streams in later, and withFallback() gives it a loading fallback.

// pages/+config.ts
import vikeReact from 'vike-react/config'
import vikeReactQuery from 'vike-react-query/config'

export default { extends: [vikeReact, vikeReactQuery], stream: true }

// pages/book/@id/Reviews.tsx
import { useSuspenseQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { withFallback } from 'vike-react-query'

export const Reviews = withFallback(
  ({ id }: { id: string }) => {
    const { data } = useSuspenseQuery({
      queryKey: ['reviews', id],
      queryFn: () => fetch(`/api/reviews/${id}`).then((r) => r.json()),
    })
    return <ul>{data.map((r: { id: string; text: string }) => <li key={r.id}>{r.text}</li>)}</ul>
  },
  () => <p>Loading reviews…</p>,
)

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Vike builds the list of a page's assets as pageContext.httpResponse.earlyHints (each entry has an earlyHintLink value), so the app does not list assets by hand. The server sends the 103 with its runtime's API, e.g. res.writeEarlyHints({ link: earlyHints.map((e) => e.earlyHintLink) }) on Node 18+. Not marked experimental or beta. (preloading)
cells.exampleHtml:
renderPage() returns the page's assets in pageContext.httpResponse.earlyHints. Pass their earlyHintLink values to the runtime's 103 API before sending the body.

// server.ts
import { renderPage } from 'vike/server'

app.get('*', async (req, res) => {
  const pageContext = await renderPage({ urlOriginal: req.originalUrl })
  const { earlyHints } = pageContext.httpResponse
  // For example with Node.js 18:
  res.writeEarlyHints({ link: earlyHints.map((e) => e.earlyHintLink) })
  // … then send pageContext.httpResponse as usual
})

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: No islands or partial hydration documented. <ClientOnly> renders a component in the browser only, which is client-only rendering. The React Server Components extension vike-react-rsc is listed as work in progress (npm 0.0.0) and is not credited. (ClientOnly, extensions)

// renderer/+config.ts
export default {
  meta: { Page: { env: { server: true, client: false } } }, // HTML-only
}

// pages/about/+Page.tsx (server only)
<div data-island="like" data-props={JSON.stringify({ bookId })}>

</div>

// pages/about/+client.tsx
import { hydrateRoot } from 'react-dom/client'
import { LikeButton } from '../../components/LikeButton'

for (const el of document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-island="like"]')) {
  hydrateRoot(el, <LikeButton {...JSON.parse(el.dataset.props!)} />)
}

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: No service worker support documented in the Vike docs or its extension list. Hand-write the worker, serve it from public/, and register it from +client.js. (static-directory, extensions)
cells.exampleHtml:
Write the worker in public/sw.js, which Vite serves at /sw.js. Register it from +client.ts.

// public/sw.js
const CACHE = 'v1'
self.addEventListener('fetch', (event) => {
  if (event.request.method !== 'GET') return
  event.respondWith(
    caches.match(event.request).then((hit) =>
      hit ?? fetch(event.request).then((res) => {
        caches.open(CACHE).then((c) => c.put(event.request, res.clone()))
        return res
      }),
    ),
  )
})
// pages/+client.ts
if ('serviceWorker' in navigator) {
  addEventListener('load', () => navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js'))
}

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: No first-party CSS inlining documented; the Document links a stylesheet imported with ?url (<link rel="stylesheet" href={styles} />). Inline by hand. (tailwind, documents)
cells.exampleHtml:
Import the stylesheet with Vite's ?inline query instead of ?url, and write it into a <style> in the Document. The Document renders only on the server, so the CSS string does not ship in a client bundle.

// src/app/Document.tsx
import styles from "./styles.css?inline"; // was: import styles from "./styles.css?url";

export const Document: React.FC<{ children: React.ReactNode }> = ({ children }) => (
  <html lang="en">
    <head>
      <meta charSet="utf-8" />
      <title>RedwoodSDK App</title>
      {/* was: <link rel="stylesheet" href={styles} /> */}
      <style dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: styles }} />
      <link rel="modulepreload" href="/src/client.tsx" />
    </head>
    <body>
      {children}
      <script>import("/src/client.tsx")</script>
    </body>
  </html>
);

cells.label: third-party
cells.bodyHtml: No first-party font handling documented; the docs show font files in public/fonts with a hand-written @font-face. The third-party route is Fontsource. (public-assets)
cells.exampleHtml:
Install a Fontsource package and import it at the top of the stylesheet. The package ships the @font-face rules and self-hosted font files, and Vite bundles them like any other CSS import.

/* src/app/styles.css */
@import "@fontsource-variable/inter";
@import "tailwindcss";

@theme {
  --font-sans: "Inter Variable", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif;
}

cells.label: third-party
cells.bodyHtml: No image component or optimizer documented; images are plain <img> tags served from public/. The third-party route is the host's Cloudflare Images transformations, wired by hand. (public-assets)
cells.exampleHtml:
Turn on Cloudflare Images transformations for the zone, then build /cdn-cgi/image/<OPTIONS>/<SOURCE> URLs by hand. This helper writes a srcSet that asks Cloudflare for each width in the best format the browser accepts.

// src/app/components/CfImage.tsx
const cf = (src: string, width: number) =>
  `/cdn-cgi/image/width=${width},quality=75,format=auto${src}`;

export function CfImage({ src, alt, width, height }: {
  src: string; alt: string; width: number; height: number;
}) {
  return (
    <img
      src={cf(src, width)}
      srcSet={[1, 2].map((d) => `${cf(src, width * d)} ${width * d}w`).join(", ")}
      sizes={`${width}px`}
      alt={alt} width={width} height={height} loading="lazy" decoding="async"
    />
  );
}

Source: Cloudflare Images: Transform via URL

artDirection.label: manual
artDirection.bodyHtml: No first-party <picture> helper documented; hand-write the markup. (public-assets)
artDirection.exampleHtml:
There is no image component, so write the <picture> by hand in a server component. Wide screens get a landscape crop and narrow screens get a square one, both served from public/. React spells the attribute srcSet.

// src/app/components/Hero.tsx
export function Hero() {
  return (
    <picture>
      {/* art direction: a square crop on narrow screens */}
      <source media="(max-width: 640px)" srcSet="/images/hero-square-640.webp"
              width={640} height={640} />
      <source media="(min-width: 641px)" srcSet="/images/hero-wide-1600.webp"
              width={1600} height={900} />
      <img src="/images/hero-wide-1600.jpg" alt="Shelves of books"
           width={1600} height={900} fetchPriority="high" decoding="async" />
    </picture>
  );
}

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: No prerender, ISR or cache API documented; set Cache-Control by hand on the response headers. The client-navigation guide says RSC payload requests are GETs so browsers and CDNs can cache them. (routing, client-side-nav)
cells.exampleHtml:
Put a small handler in front of the page in the route's array and set Cache-Control on response.headers. The browser and Cloudflare's edge then cache the HTML for that route.

// src/worker.tsx
import { defineApp } from "rwsdk/worker";
import { render, route } from "rwsdk/router";
import { Document } from "@/app/Document";
import { BookPage } from "@/app/pages/BookPage";

export default defineApp([
  render(Document, [
    route("/books/:id", [
      ({ response }) => {
        response.headers.set("Cache-Control", "public, max-age=60, s-maxage=300");
      },
      BookPage,
    ]),
  ]),
]);

Source: RedwoodSDK: Request Handling, Routing & Responses

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: With client-side navigation on, <link rel="x-prefetch" href="/about" /> makes RedwoodSDK fetch that route in the background after each navigation and store the response in the browser Cache API. Needs the onHydrated callback from initClientNavigation(). No hover or viewport trigger documented. (client-side-nav)
cells.exampleHtml:
Turn on client navigation and pass onHydrated to initClient. Then render <link rel="x-prefetch"> for likely next routes. RedwoodSDK fetches each one after navigation and keeps it in the Cache API.

// src/client.tsx
import { initClient, initClientNavigation } from "rwsdk/client";

const { handleResponse, onHydrated } = initClientNavigation();
initClient({ handleResponse, onHydrated });
// src/app/pages/BlogListPage.tsx
import { link } from "@/shared/links";

export function BlogListPage({ posts }) {
  return posts.map((post) => {
    const href = link("/blog/:slug", { slug: post.slug });
    return (
      <article key={post.id}>
        <link rel="x-prefetch" href={href} />
        <a href={href}><h2>{post.title}</h2></a>
      </article>
    );
  });
}

Source: RedwoodSDK: Client Side Navigation

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Server components are "rendered on the server as HTML and then streamed to the client". Wrap an async server component in <Suspense fallback={...}> to show a loading state while its data is fetched. Nothing to enable. (react-server-components)
cells.exampleHtml:
Make a server component async and wrap it in <Suspense>. The page shell streams first with the fallback, and the list streams in when the query resolves.

// src/app/pages/todos/TodoPage.tsx
import { Suspense } from "react";

export async function Todos({ ctx }) {
  const todos = await db.todo.findMany({ where: { userId: ctx.user.id } });
  return <ol>{todos.map((todo) => <li key={todo.id}>{todo.title}</li>)}</ol>;
}

export async function TodoPage({ ctx }) {
  return (
    <div>
      <h1>Todos</h1>
      <Suspense fallback={<div>Loading...</div>}>
        <Todos ctx={ctx} />
      </Suspense>
    </div>
  );
}

Source: RedwoodSDK: React Server Components

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: No first-party preload Link headers or 103 Early Hints documented; the Document example hand-writes <link rel="modulepreload" href="/src/client.tsx" />. Set a Link header by hand with requestInfo.response.headers in middleware. (documents, routing)
cells.exampleHtml:
Add a middleware that sets a Link header on every response. This one preloads a font from public/, whose URL does not change between builds. Cloudflare can turn Link preload headers into 103 Early Hints when Early Hints is on for the zone.

// src/app/headers.ts
import type { RouteMiddleware } from "rwsdk/worker";

export const preloadHeaders = (): RouteMiddleware => ({ response }) => {
  response.headers.append(
    "Link",
    "</fonts/brand-font.woff2>; rel=preload; as=font; type=font/woff2; crossorigin",
  );
};

// src/worker.tsx
export default defineApp([
  preloadHeaders(),
  render(Document, [route("/", HomePage)]),
]);

Source: RedwoodSDK: Security · Cloudflare: Early Hints

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: React Server Components are the default; only components marked "use client" ship JavaScript and hydrate. (react-server-components)
cells.exampleHtml:
Pages are server components by default and send no JavaScript. Only the component marked "use client" ships code and hydrates.

// src/app/components/LikeButton.tsx
"use client";
import { useState } from "react";

export function LikeButton() {
  const [likes, setLikes] = useState(0);
  return <button onClick={() => setLikes(likes + 1)}>Like ({likes})</button>;
}

// src/app/pages/BookPage.tsx (server component, no client JS of its own)
import { LikeButton } from "@/app/components/LikeButton";

export async function BookPage({ params }) {
  const book = await getBook(params.id);
  return (
    <article>
      <h1>{book.title}</h1>
      <p>{book.description}</p>
      <LikeButton />
    </article>
  );
}

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: render(Document, routes, { ssr: false }) renders a group of routes on the client only, and { rscPayload: false } serves a group as static HTML with no hydration. No build-time prerender documented. (sdk-router)
cells.exampleHtml:
Pass options as the third argument to render(). rscPayload: false serves a group as static HTML with no hydration, and ssr: false renders client components only in the browser.

// src/worker.tsx
import { defineApp } from "rwsdk/worker";
import { render, prefix } from "rwsdk/router";
import { ReactDocument, StaticDocument } from "@/app/Document";

export default defineApp([
  // Default: SSR with the RSC payload, so the page hydrates
  render(ReactDocument, [prefix("/app", appRoutes)]),
  // Static HTML, no hydration (StaticDocument has no client script)
  render(StaticDocument, [prefix("/docs", docsRoutes)], { rscPayload: false }),
  // Client components render only in the browser
  render(ReactDocument, [prefix("/spa", spaRoutes)], { ssr: false }),
]);

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: React-based; the RedwoodSDK guide adds the first-party React Compiler as a Babel plugin on @vitejs/plugin-react, placed before the Cloudflare and RedwoodSDK plugins. (react-compiler)
cells.exampleHtml:
Add the React Compiler as a Babel plugin on @vitejs/plugin-react, placed before the Cloudflare and RedwoodSDK plugins. Components then get automatic memoization without useMemo or useCallback.

// vite.config.mts
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import { redwood } from "rwsdk/vite";
import { cloudflare } from "@cloudflare/vite-plugin";
import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    react({
      babel: {
        plugins: ["babel-plugin-react-compiler"],
      },
    }),
    cloudflare({ viteEnvironment: { name: "worker" } }),
    redwood(),
  ],
});

cells.bodyHtml: No first-party analyzer documented; RedwoodSDK is a Vite plugin, so the third-party route is a community visualizer such as rollup-plugin-visualizer. (hosting)

RedwoodSDK builds with Vite, so add rollup-plugin-visualizer to the plugins. The build writes stats.html with a treemap of the bundles.

import { defineConfig, type PluginOption } from "vite";
import { redwood } from "rwsdk/vite";
import { cloudflare } from "@cloudflare/vite-plugin";
import { visualizer } from "rollup-plugin-visualizer";

    cloudflare({ viteEnvironment: { name: "worker" } }),
    redwood(),
    visualizer({ filename: "stats.html", gzipSize: true }) as PluginOption,

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: No first-party script-loading strategy documented; scripts go in the Document by hand, and the security page covers only the CSP nonce they need. (documents, security)
cells.exampleHtml:
Write the tags in the Document yourself. An external script gets async, and an inline snippet needs the per-request rw.nonce to pass the CSP. Add the script's host to script-src in src/app/headers.ts.

// src/app/Document.tsx
export const Document = ({ rw, children }) => (
  <html lang="en">
    <head>
      {/* … */}
      <script async src="https://plausible.io/js/script.js" data-domain="books.example" />
    </head>
    <body>
      {children}
      <script nonce={rw.nonce}>
        {`window.plausible = window.plausible || function () { (plausible.q = plausible.q || []).push(arguments) };`}
      </script>
      <script>import("/src/client.tsx")</script>
    </body>
  </html>
);

cells.bodyHtml: Cloudflare Workers is the only documented host; no Node, Vercel or Netlify target is documented. (hosting)
